guides.title: What is SAM (Smart Auto Manager)?
guides.body:
**SAM (Smart Auto Manager)** helps a vehicle workshop organise customers, vehicles, repairs, parts, invoices and payments. Owners can review the business, service advisors can coordinate visits, technicians can record their work, and authorised staff can manage billing.

## How the main records fit together

- **Customer** — What it means: The person or company you serve. What normally comes next: Add their vehicle.
- **Vehicle** — What it means: The vehicle and its service details. What normally comes next: Book a visit or open a work order.
- **Service booking** — What it means: A requested appointment. What normally comes next: Confirm it and convert it when the vehicle arrives.
- **Work order** — What it means: The vehicle's visit, complaint and coverage. What normally comes next: Inspect the vehicle and add an estimate or job order.
- **Estimate** — What it means: The proposed work and price. What normally comes next: Obtain agreement, then convert it to a job order.
- **Job order** — What it means: The tasks, packages, parts and technician work. What normally comes next: Approve the cost, complete the work and approve it.
- **Invoice** — What it means: The customer's bill. What normally comes next: Issue it, then record payment.

An appointment is optional: you can open a work order for a walk-in. A work order can have more than one job order. An estimate is useful when the customer must agree to a price before work starts.

## Choose your starting point

- New workshop: follow [Your first workshop job](/help/en/autoserv-pro/first-workshop-job).
- Reception or service advisor: start with [customers](/help/en/autoserv-pro/create-and-manage-customers) and [work orders](/help/en/autoserv-pro/create-and-manage-work-orders).
- Technician: open [Track technician work](/help/en/autoserv-pro/track-technician-work).
- Billing staff: read [Create and issue an invoice](/help/en/autoserv-pro/create-and-issue-an-invoice).

## Access and editions

Your workshop's permissions and subscription determine the screens and actions you can use. A missing option does not necessarily mean something is broken. The hosted edition includes **Plan & Billing**; a standalone installation does not have the same subscription screens.

Vehicle owners use the workshop's separate customer portal or the individual links staff share with them. They do not need a staff account to open a shared inspection or tracking link.

## Related articles

- [Dashboard and navigation](/help/en/autoserv-pro/dashboard-and-navigation)
- [Roles and permissions](/help/en/autoserv-pro/roles-and-permissions)

guides.title: Complete your first workshop job
guides.body:
Use this guide to take your first customer from reception to an issued invoice and payment. Work on the correct workshop account and use real records only when you are ready to operate the business.

## Before you begin

The person completing each stage needs permission for that action. You may hand the job from an advisor to a technician, manager and cashier. Have the customer's contact details, vehicle information, agreed work and prices ready.

## Set up the essentials

1. Sign in using your workshop's staff login address.
2. Open **Configuration → Company Settings**. Check the business name, contact details, currency and timezone. Click **Save Changes**.
3. Ask an authorised colleague to check **Configuration → Numbering** and **Finance → Accounts** before issuing documents or taking money.
4. Add the technicians who will work on the vehicle through **Configuration → Employees**. They need the **Technician** role and a working login.
5. Prepare the labour tasks, packages and parts you expect to use. Stock already on the shelf can be entered when a product is first created.

## Take the customer through the visit

1. Open **Customers → Customers**, search first, then use **Add Customer** if needed. Enter the name and phone number and click **Save**.
2. Open **Customers → Vehicles** and use **Add Vehicle**. Select the customer and enter the plate, make and model.
3. Open **Operations → Work Orders → Add Work Order**. Select the customer and vehicle, enter the visit details and complaint, then click **Save**.
4. Record photos or start an inspection if needed. Use an estimate when the price still needs agreement.
5. Add a job order with the required **Labour Tasks**, **Service Packages** and **Parts / Items**. Check quantities and prices, then click **Save**.
6. Once the price is agreed, an authorised colleague uses **Approve Cost**. Assign a technician to the job's work.
7. The technician records their work using **Start Timer**, **Stop Timer** and **Finish Task**.
8. Review the completed work and use **Approve Work**.
9. Use **Add Invoice**, check all lines, discounts, tax, advances and the total. Use **Save as Draft** if another person must review it; use **Issue** only when it is correct.
10. On the issued invoice, use **Record Payment** for money actually received. A partial payment leaves a balance due.

## What happens next

Issuing assigns the final invoice number and locks the billed job order. Payment records the receipt separately. Vehicle collection is still an operational handover: confirm the vehicle has actually been collected before recording that fact, and release its bay when it leaves.

## If you cannot continue

An unavailable approval or payment button usually requires a different permission or an earlier workflow step. Ask the colleague responsible for that stage rather than changing a status to skip it.

## Related articles

- [Create and approve job orders](/help/en/autoserv-pro/create-and-approve-job-orders)
- [Create and issue an invoice](/help/en/autoserv-pro/create-and-issue-an-invoice)
- [Roles and permissions](/help/en/autoserv-pro/roles-and-permissions)

guides.title: Sign in or reset your staff password
guides.body:
Use your workshop's staff login page to access SAM. This is different from the customer portal used by vehicle owners.

## Sign in

1. Open the workshop address supplied by your administrator.
2. Enter your **Email Address** and **Password**.
3. Use **Sign In**. Only select **Remember me for 30 days** on a device you control.
4. If your workshop provides **Login with Orions360**, you can use that route with the connected Orions360 account. Its availability depends on the installation.

Your permissions determine which dashboard and menu items appear. Technicians normally use the **My Work** screens.

## Accept an employee access link

1. Open the access message sent by your administrator.
2. Follow its link and enter a **New Password** and **Confirm Password**.
3. Use **Set password and sign in**.

Employee access links work once and expire after 48 hours. Renewing a link makes the older link unusable. Ask your administrator to renew it if it has expired.

## Reset a forgotten password

1. Select **Forgot Password?** on the staff login screen.
2. Enter your **Email Address** and use **Send Password Reset Link**.
3. Open the newest reset email and follow the instructions. The password form asks for at least eight characters.
4. If prompted to verify your email, open the verification message or use **Resend Verification Email**.

## Troubleshooting

If no message arrives, check the address and spam folder, then ask your administrator to check the workshop's email delivery. Repeatedly requesting links can make it harder to identify the newest one.

A successful login with missing screens is an access issue, not a reason to reset the password. An expired trial or suspended account can also restrict what you can do.

## Related articles

- [Add employees and share access](/help/en/autoserv-pro/add-employees-and-share-access)
- [Login, access and plan problems](/help/en/autoserv-pro/login-access-and-plan-problems)

guides.title: Find your next task in SAM
guides.body:
The dashboard gives you a starting point for the workshop's activity. What you can see depends on your role, permissions and plan. Financial figures can be withheld even when operational figures are available.

## Start your day

1. Open **Dashboard** and check the selected date range before interpreting its figures.
2. Review work waiting for attention, appointments, ongoing work and completed vehicles awaiting the next step.
3. Open the relevant record from an available dashboard link, or use its list in the sidebar.
4. Review your notifications. Open the linked item before deciding whether it still needs action; its status may have changed since the notification was created.

## Use the sidebar

- **Operations** — Work Orders, Job Orders, Service Bookings, Estimates and Invoices.
- **Customers** — Customer and vehicle records.
- **Workshop** — Labour Tasks, Service Packages, Job Templates, Bay Board, PM Board, Fleet and Insurance Claims.
- **Inventory** — Products, stock, suppliers, purchases and parts requests.
- **Finance** — Money movements, expenses, income and supplier payments.
- **Reports** — Detailed operational and financial views.
- **Configuration** — Employees, access, company details and connected services.

Technicians have a **My Work** section containing **My Dashboard**, **My Tasks**, **Parts Requests** and **Time Log**. The **User Guide** link is available independently of the operational permissions.

## Search a list

Open the correct list, use **Search** and any available status or date filters, then check the pagination controls. Clear the filters before concluding that a record is missing. A product, customer or employee picker may require you to type before it returns matches.

## What happens next

Opening a record shows its current state and available actions. A dashboard count is a summary, not permission to approve, invoice or pay the items behind it.

## Troubleshooting

If a number differs from a report, compare the date range and what the two screens count. Work dates, invoice dates and payment dates represent different events. Do not treat an unavailable figure as zero.

## Related articles

- [Workshop and sales reports](/help/en/autoserv-pro/workshop-and-sales-reports)
- [Roles and permissions](/help/en/autoserv-pro/roles-and-permissions)

guides.title: Create and manage customers
guides.body:
A customer record connects the person's or company's vehicles, workshop visits and billing details. Search before creating a record to avoid splitting one customer's history across duplicates.

## Add a customer

1. Open **Customers → Customers** and search by name, phone, email or TRN.
2. Select **Add Customer** if no suitable record exists.
3. Enter **Customer Name** and **Phone**. Both are required; the phone field accepts up to 20 characters.
4. Add **Company Name**, **Email**, **TRN (Tax Registration No.)** and the address when relevant. Check the email carefully if the customer will receive documents or use the portal.
5. Set **How did they find us?** to the source you actually know. This supports the Acquisition Source report.
6. Choose **Customer Group** or **Price Group** if your workshop uses them.
7. Under **Billing**, choose the agreed **Credit Terms** and click **Save**.

Credit terms include **Cash (no credit terms)**, **Due on receipt** and the available Net-day terms. Due on receipt means zero days; it is different from leaving credit terms unset. New invoices can derive their due date from the customer's terms when no due date is supplied.

## Update an existing customer

Open the customer's record or use its edit action, change the relevant details, and click **Save**. Keep contact details current before sharing a tracking, estimate or portal link.

Do not enter historical debt in **Opening Balance** without checking with your administrator. This field is also used by the customer deposit feature; it should not be treated as a general unpaid-invoice balance.

## What happens next

The customer becomes available when adding vehicles and work orders. Creating a staff user is a separate process. For customer portal access, use **Set Portal Password** and follow the portal guide.

## Troubleshooting

An invalid email or missing name/phone prevents saving. If the correct record does not appear in a picker, clear the search and check that you are in the right workshop. Avoid deleting a customer as a way to resolve duplicate financial history.

[Screenshot: Customer form showing identity, contact details and Credit Terms, using synthetic data.]

## Related articles

- [Add and manage vehicles](/help/en/autoserv-pro/add-and-manage-vehicles)
- [Customer portal](/help/en/autoserv-pro/customer-portal)

guides.title: Add a vehicle and find its service history
guides.body:
Each vehicle belongs to a customer. Confirm both the owner and the plate before creating work, especially when several similar vehicles visit the workshop.

## Add a vehicle

1. Open **Customers → Vehicles** and search for the plate first.
2. Select **Add Vehicle**.
3. Select the customer, then enter **Plate Number**, **Make** and **Model**. These are required.
4. Add the year, **Vehicle Type**, colour and **Chassis No. (VIN)** where known.
5. Record the **Odometer (km)** and **Fuel Type**. For an electric or plug-in hybrid vehicle, complete the relevant battery information if available.
6. Add **Mulkiya Expiry**, **RTA Fitness Expiry**, **Next Service Date** or **Next Service Mileage (km)** when your workshop tracks them.
7. Click **Save** and reopen the record to check the details.

Do not guess missing identifiers or readings. The plate can contain up to 50 characters; make and model can each contain up to 100.

## Review a vehicle

Open the vehicle to review its service history and available handover information. Use **Edit Vehicle** to correct current details. Updating a reminder field is different from configuring a recurring PM schedule.

Where a plate-scan control is available, treat recognition as a starting point. Check every recognised character and select the correct existing vehicle before continuing. A scan does not prove ownership.

## What happens next

The vehicle can be selected on a work order for its customer. The fuel type helps staff identify when EV information is relevant. Use the actual odometer reading at each visit; changing the vehicle record alone does not perform or complete a service.

## Troubleshooting

If a duplicate-plate warning appears, inspect the existing record before adding another. If **Vehicle Types** is visible but access is refused, ask an administrator to check your settings permissions. Deactivating a vehicle is different from deleting its service history.

## Related articles

- [Create and manage customers](/help/en/autoserv-pro/create-and-manage-customers)
- [Create and manage work orders](/help/en/autoserv-pro/create-and-manage-work-orders)
- [Maintenance and driver handovers](/help/en/autoserv-pro/maintenance-and-driver-handovers)

guides.title: Request a service appointment online
guides.body:
Use the booking link supplied by your workshop to request a visit. You do not need a staff login. Have your phone number, vehicle details and a short description of the problem ready.

## Make a booking request

1. Open the workshop's booking link and check that the workshop name is correct.
2. Choose a date on the calendar, then select an available time slot. Slots marked **Full** cannot be selected.
3. Select **Continue to Details**.
4. If you have visited before, use **Phone · Email · Plate — enter to look up your record** and carefully confirm the displayed identity and vehicle. Use **Not you? Clear** if the result is wrong.
5. Enter your **Full Name** and **Phone Number**. Email is optional.
6. Check **Vehicle Details**, including the plate, make and model, and explain **What brings you in?**
7. Add any relevant **Optional details**, review the date and slot, then use **Confirm Booking** once.
8. Keep the booking reference from the result screen.

## What happens next

Your request appears in the workshop's Service Bookings list. The result page currently says **Booking Confirmed!**, but the workshop still has a separate confirmation step. Contact the workshop if you need certainty before travelling.

Submitting a request does not create a completed repair or an invoice. Staff can convert it into a work order when the visit is ready to begin.

## Troubleshooting

- **No slots available:** choose another date or contact the workshop.
- **The slot just became fully booked:** another request filled it while you were entering your details. Select another time.
- **Missing required details:** enter your name and phone and check the highlighted fields. The service description allows up to 1,000 characters.
- **Unsure whether submission succeeded:** check for a reference or contact the workshop before submitting again.

## Related articles

- [Customer portal](/help/en/autoserv-pro/customer-portal)
- [Frequently asked questions](/help/en/autoserv-pro/frequently-asked-questions)

guides.title: Confirm a booking and turn it into a work order
guides.body:
Service Bookings holds appointment requests from the public booking form. Viewing bookings and managing them are separate permissions.

## Review and confirm

1. Open **Operations → Service Bookings → Bookings**.
2. Find the request and check the date, slot, customer, vehicle and service description.
3. Use **Confirm** when the appointment is accepted.
4. Use **Delay** or **Cancel** if the visit cannot proceed as planned. Coordinate any replacement time with the customer.

Confirm attempts a WhatsApp update. Delay and Cancel attempt an SMS update. These actions depend on the connected messaging service; a saved status alone is not proof that the customer received a message.

## Start the workshop visit

1. Check that the booking has not already been converted and that no work order already represents this visit.
2. Select **Convert to Work Order**.
3. Review the result. Use **Open Work Order** to continue or **Stay Here** to return to bookings.
4. Check the customer, vehicle, complaint, mileage and coverage on the created work order before adding repair work.

Conversion can find or create the customer and vehicle using the booking details. A typo or a different phone-number format can therefore lead to a duplicate record. Correct the resulting record before sending private customer information.

## Share the booking form

Use **Share booking link** to obtain a link for a customer. The staff screen does not provide a separate verified **New Service Booking** form; the public form is the booking entry point.

## What happens next

The booking becomes a converted visit linked to a work order. Inspection, estimates, technician work, invoicing and payment continue on the workshop records.

## Troubleshooting

Do not repeatedly convert a booking after a slow response. Search Work Orders first: the current conversion flow needs extra care around retries. If Confirm is missing despite being able to view bookings, ask for booking-management permission.

## Related articles

- [Set booking hours and holidays](/help/en/autoserv-pro/set-booking-hours-and-holidays)
- [Create and manage work orders](/help/en/autoserv-pro/create-and-manage-work-orders)

guides.title: Set booking slots and workshop holidays
guides.body:
Configure the times customers can request through the booking form. You need permission to manage Service Bookings.

## Add a time slot

1. Open **Operations → Service Bookings → Slots**.
2. Select **Add Slot**.
3. In **Add Time Slot**, enter **Start Time**, **End Time** and **Slot Label**.
4. Set **Max Bookings Per Slot** and choose **Active Days**.
5. Click **Save**, then check the slot on the public booking form.

The end time must be after the start time. Capacity must be between 1 and 99. Use a label customers can understand, such as a clear time range. Use the slot's edit action to change it and **Activate** or **Deactivate** to control availability.

## Add an off day

1. Open **Off Days** and select **Add Off Day / Holiday**.
2. Choose **Recurring Weekly** for a regular closed day, or **Specific Date / Holiday** for one date.
3. Choose the weekday or date and enter a **Label / Reason**.
4. Use **Add** and check the relevant list.

A new specific-date holiday must be today or later. Removing an off-day entry makes that date eligible for booking again, subject to the remaining schedule.

## What happens next

The public form uses the slot and off-day settings to display available choices. Existing appointments still need staff attention: changing hours is not a substitute for contacting customers whose accepted visit is affected.

## Troubleshooting

If a date has no slots, check its active weekdays, holidays, capacity and whether today's times have already passed. After changing a schedule, reopen the public form to verify the result. Avoid deleting a slot merely to rearrange an existing customer's appointment.

## Related articles

- [Request a service appointment online](/help/en/autoserv-pro/book-a-service-online)
- [Manage service bookings](/help/en/autoserv-pro/manage-service-bookings)

guides.title: Create and manage a work order
guides.body:
A work order records one workshop visit: who brought the vehicle, what needs attention and how the visit is progressing. The detailed repair tasks and parts belong to its job orders.

## Before you begin

Have the correct customer and vehicle records ready. You need work-order creation permission; editing, photos and customer tracking links can require additional permissions.

## Create the visit

1. Open **Operations → Work Orders → Add Work Order**.
2. Select **Customers** and the correct vehicle. Use **Add Customer** or **Add Vehicle** if a required record is missing, and check the new record before continuing.
3. Enter **WO Date** and **WO Type**, then record **Mileage (km)**.
4. Describe the customer's concern in **Reported Defect / Complaint**.
5. Add **Promised Date**, **LPO number**, **Service Advisor** and **Priority** when relevant. Mark **Customer Waiting** only when the customer is actually waiting.
6. Put staff-only context in **Internal Notes**.
7. Complete **Coverage / Claims** if the visit is under warranty, insurance or contract. Selecting coverage does not itself approve a claim.
8. Click **Save**. The new work order starts **Open** and receives its number automatically.

## Continue the visit

Use **Start inspection** to record findings, **Add Job Order** to prepare work, or **Print job card** for a workshop document. Add intake photographs before repair where useful.

Update the status to reflect the real situation. Waiting for parts, waiting for approval and completed work are different conditions. Job progress can advance a parent work order automatically; check the parent record after important changes.

## What happens next

The work order connects the visit's inspection, estimates, work and invoices. An **Invoiced** work-order status cannot be moved back through the editor. Issued job orders are locked financial records.

## Troubleshooting

Deletion is blocked when an advance is attached or an associated job has been invoiced. Do not delete a visit to undo a payment. If a saved coverage detail looks wrong, reopen the record and verify it before relying on it.

## Related articles

- [Inspect a vehicle](/help/en/autoserv-pro/inspect-a-vehicle)
- [Create and approve job orders](/help/en/autoserv-pro/create-and-approve-job-orders)
- [Advances and bulk payments](/help/en/autoserv-pro/advances-and-bulk-payments)

guides.title: Record a vehicle inspection and photos
guides.body:
An inspection records what was checked and what was found. It can later be shared with the customer or used to prepare an estimate for flagged items.

## Before you begin

Open the correct work order. Your workshop needs an active inspection template. Recording, completing and sharing inspections are separate permissions; technician access can also depend on assigned work.

## Record the findings

1. Open the work order and select **Start inspection**.
2. If **Which inspection?** appears, choose the checklist suited to the visit.
3. Work through the sections. Record each checkpoint's verdict, reading and **Note (optional)** as appropriate.
4. Use **Pass**, **Attention** or **Fail** to describe the finding. A reading can suggest a verdict; review it against what you actually observed.
5. Associate relevant photographs with the findings where the screen allows it.
6. Use **Save** to keep the inspection editable and continue later.
7. When the record is ready, select **Complete inspection** and review any warning about blank checkpoints.

## Completion is final for that inspection

Completing freezes the inspection. Blank checkpoints cannot be filled afterwards. Start a new inspection for a re-check rather than trying to rewrite the completed record.

**Estimate from findings** creates quote lines from items marked Attention or Fail. It does not price the repair for you: review the task description, hours, rate, parts and total before sharing the estimate.

## Photos and EV information

The work order's **Upload Photos** action accepts up to ten images in one upload, each up to 8 MB. Avoid customer identity documents or unrelated personal information in photographs you may share.

For an EV visit, complete the relevant **EV High-Voltage Service Checklist** and use **Save EV Checklist**. This is a record for qualified workshop staff; the application checklist is not a substitute for the vehicle manufacturer's repair procedure or required training.

## Troubleshooting

If no template is available, ask an authorised colleague to check **Configuration → Inspection Templates**. If there is nothing to quote, record a genuine Attention or Fail finding first. Do not mark a sound component faulty merely to enable the estimate action.

[Screenshot: Inspection checklist with a reading, an Attention finding and the Save and Complete inspection actions, using a sample vehicle.]

## Related articles

- [Share progress and inspections](/help/en/autoserv-pro/share-progress-and-inspections)
- [Configure inspection templates](/help/en/autoserv-pro/configure-inspection-templates)

guides.title: Share vehicle progress or inspection findings
guides.body:
Tracking and inspection links let a customer see information about their visit without a staff account. Choose the link that matches what you want to explain.

## Share progress

1. Open the correct work order and verify the customer and phone number.
2. Review the current status and any information intended for the customer.
3. Use **Send Tracking Link**.
4. Read the result carefully. The link may be sent through WhatsApp or copied for you to send manually.

If the customer has no phone number or WhatsApp fails, a copied link is not a delivered message. Paste it into the conversation with the correct customer yourself.

## Share an inspection

1. Open the inspection and check its findings, readings and photos.
2. Save the recorded work and select **Share with customer**.
3. Review the sharing prompt and use the offered customer message or link.
4. Explain any flagged items in language the customer can understand. Use an estimate for the proposed price and work.

Anyone with a shared link can open its customer-facing content. Check that photographs contain only information appropriate for the vehicle owner before sharing. Avoid sending a link into a group conversation unless that is intentional.

## What happens next

The customer can review progress or findings. Opening a tracking or inspection link does not automatically pay an invoice or authorise every proposed repair. Estimate approval is a separate workflow.

## Troubleshooting

- A missing share action can mean your account lacks tracking or inspection-sharing permission.
- If the customer sees the wrong vehicle, stop using the link and verify the work order and contact before sending another.
- If the page is unavailable, ask staff to reopen the source record and obtain the appropriate current link.

## Related articles

- [Inspect a vehicle](/help/en/autoserv-pro/inspect-a-vehicle)
- [Create and send an estimate](/help/en/autoserv-pro/create-and-send-an-estimate)
- [Email, WhatsApp and link problems](/help/en/autoserv-pro/email-whatsapp-and-link-problems)

guides.title: Create an estimate and obtain customer agreement
guides.body:
An estimate explains the proposed work and price before the repair proceeds. It belongs to a work order. Creating, editing, sending and converting estimates require separate permissions.

## Prepare the estimate

1. Create or open the work order for the visit.
2. Open **Operations → Estimates → Add Estimate** and select the work order.
3. Set **JO Date** and **Job Type** where applicable.
4. Add the required **Labour Tasks**, **Service Packages** and **Parts / Items**.
5. Check descriptions, hours, prices, quantities and the total. An estimate created from inspection findings starts with unpriced task lines that need review.
6. Click **Save**, then reopen the estimate to check the saved result.

Saved parts and package lines can affect stock availability in the current workflow. An estimate should not be used as a scratchpad for arbitrary stock quantities.

## Send it to the customer

1. Check the customer and proposed work, then use **Send**.
2. Read whether the approval link was sent on WhatsApp or only copied.
3. If it was only copied, send it to the correct customer manually.
4. Review the customer's response before starting work. When a visit has multiple estimates or has been revised, confirm that the customer is agreeing to the exact work and price you intend to perform.

## Convert agreed work

Use **Convert to JO** when the estimate is ready to become live work. Conversion cannot be undone through the same action. A rejected estimate can show **Convert anyway**; only proceed if the customer has since agreed through a separate conversation.

Customer acceptance, conversion and **Approve Cost** are distinct steps. Review the resulting job order and arrange staff cost approval before technicians proceed under your workshop's workflow.

## What happens next

The converted record appears as a job order. Assign technicians, complete the work, obtain **Approve Work**, then create the invoice.

## Troubleshooting

An invoiced record cannot be converted or edited as an open quote. If an approval link shows unexpected work, do not ask the customer to approve it; contact your administrator to resolve the quote/visit association.

## Related articles

- [Inspection to approved repair](/help/en/autoserv-pro/inspection-to-approved-repair)
- [Create and approve job orders](/help/en/autoserv-pro/create-and-approve-job-orders)

guides.title: Create a job order and approve the work
guides.body:
A job order holds the actual repair work: labour tasks, packages, parts and technician time. Each job order belongs to a work order.

## Add the work

1. Open the visit and choose **Add Job Order**, or use **Operations → Job Orders → Add Job Order**.
2. Select the work order and set **JO Date** and **Job Type**.
3. Use **Add Labour Task** and review **Estimated Hours**, **Actual Hours** and **Normal Rate**. Do not assume a displayed hour value is a completed technician time entry.
4. Use **Add Service Package** for bundled work. Review its package price and included items.
5. Use **Add Item** under **Parts / Items** for separately charged parts. Check the product, unit, quantity and unit price.
6. Click **Save** and read any stock-shortfall warning.

Saving can allocate stock. A backorder warning means the job was saved with a shortfall, not that the missing parts have arrived.

## Approval and execution

1. Once the customer agrees to the price, use **Approve Cost** if you have permission.
2. Use **Assign Technician** to add the selected technician to every task and package on the job. A selectable technician must have an employee record linked to a user with the Technician role.
3. Have technicians complete the assigned work and record their time.
4. Review the finished tasks and use **Approve Work** to sign off the result.
5. Use **Add Invoice** when the job is ready for billing.

Cost approval and work approval are different responsibilities. The system refuses work approval before cost approval. The normal invoice entry flow expects the work to be signed off.

## What happens next

The job becomes ready for invoicing. Issuing its invoice locks the job against further repair edits. If it needs additional work before invoicing, use the authorised rework process rather than pretending it remained approved.

## Troubleshooting

If a technician is missing, check their employee/user link and role. If the product unit is refused, choose a compatible unit from the product's measurement family. If the job is already invoiced, stop editing and ask the billing administrator how to handle the correction.

## Related articles

- [Track technician work](/help/en/autoserv-pro/track-technician-work)
- [Rework and completion](/help/en/autoserv-pro/rework-and-completion)
- [Create and issue an invoice](/help/en/autoserv-pro/create-and-issue-an-invoice)

guides.title: Assign technicians and record their working time
guides.body:
Technician time helps the workshop understand progress and labour use. Each technician needs an employee profile linked to their staff account and must be assigned to the work.

## Assign a technician

An authorised advisor or manager can use **Assign Technician** on a job order. This action assigns the selected person across its tasks and service packages. Confirm the intended scope before using it on a job shared by several technicians.

## Work as a technician

1. Open **My Work → My Tasks**, or the **Assigned Tasks** area of **My Dashboard**.
2. Find the correct job and task or package. Check the vehicle and work description before starting.
3. Select **Start Timer** when you begin working.
4. Use **Stop Timer** when you pause or move away from that work.
5. Resume when appropriate, then use **Finish Task** when the task is actually complete.
6. Open **Time Log** to review recorded sessions.

Only one task or package timer can run for a technician at a time. Starting another while one is running produces a message identifying the existing work. Stop or finish that work before starting the next timer.

## Understand performance figures

**Utilisation** compares clocked time with available working time. **Productivity** compares billed time with available time. **Efficiency** compares the work's flat-rate time with clocked time. Check the date range and employee working-time settings before comparing figures.

These figures answer different questions. A missing figure or restricted report is not a zero performance result.

## What happens next

Finished tasks contribute to job progress. A manager still needs to inspect the completed work and approve it before the normal billing step. Removing a technician assignment keeps their past time records.

## Troubleshooting

- **No technician profile found:** ask an administrator to check the employee/user link.
- **You are not assigned:** ask the advisor to assign the correct task or package.
- **Already invoiced and locked:** additional time cannot be started against that billed job.
- Incorrect recorded hours should be reviewed by an authorised manager; do not manufacture timer sessions to compensate.

## Related articles

- [Add employees and share access](/help/en/autoserv-pro/add-employees-and-share-access)
- [Request and issue parts](/help/en/autoserv-pro/request-and-issue-parts)
- [Rework and completion](/help/en/autoserv-pro/rework-and-completion)

guides.title: Reopen unfinished work or complete a job
guides.body:
Use rework when a job needs to return to technicians before it is invoiced. Use forced completion only when an authorised person has deliberately verified the work outside the normal technician sign-off flow.

## Send a job for rework

1. Open **Operations → Job Orders** and review the job.
2. Confirm that it has not been invoiced. Ask technicians to stop active timers before resetting the job.
3. Use **Rework** and read the confirmation carefully.
4. Confirm only when you intend to reopen every task and package on that job.
5. Reassign technicians where needed and check the related work order's status.

Rework withdraws work approval and resets task completion and recorded task actual-hour values to zero. Historical time sessions remain for reporting. Rework is therefore not a small edit to one finished task; review hours and costs again after the repeated work.

## Force completion

1. Review what remains incomplete and verify that the work really is finished.
2. Use **Force Complete**.
3. Read **Force Complete All Tasks** and confirm the number of remaining items.
4. Perform the normal quality review and **Approve Work** step.

Force completion marks the remaining tasks and packages complete without technician sign-off. It does not prove that a technician performed them or that their time has been recorded correctly.

## What happens next

A reworked job returns to the execution flow and needs work approval again. A completed and approved job can proceed to an invoice. Once issued, the job is locked; rework is not a way to reopen a financial record.

## Troubleshooting

If a timer or parent work-order status still looks inconsistent after rework, stop and ask the manager to review it. Avoid repeated resets, which make reconciliation harder. For a billed repair that needs a return visit, ask the advisor to record the new visit and any warranty arrangement through the workshop's approved process.

## Related articles

- [Track technician work](/help/en/autoserv-pro/track-technician-work)
- [Create and approve job orders](/help/en/autoserv-pro/create-and-approve-job-orders)

guides.title: See which vehicles occupy your workshop bays
guides.body:
The **Bay Board** shows where vehicles are on the workshop floor. A bay assignment records location; it does not itself complete, invoice or close the vehicle's work order.

## Set up bays

1. Open **Workshop → Bay Board**.
2. Use **Add First Bay** or **Add Bay** if you have bay-management permission.
3. Enter a unique **Bay Name**, choose **Bay Type**, add any **Notes**, then select **Save Bay**.

The bay type affects the time-limit indicator. Choose the real use of the bay rather than a type that makes its warning disappear.

## Assign and release a vehicle

1. On an available bay, use **Assign**.
2. Select the work order for the vehicle physically entering that bay.
3. Check the board after saving, particularly when another staff member is also moving vehicles.
4. Use **Assign technician** if the appropriate person should be added to the active work order's tasks.
5. When the vehicle leaves, use **Release** and confirm **Empty bay**.

Check the destination before moving a vehicle. Release an occupied target deliberately rather than assuming a move will preserve its existing occupant.

## Read the indicators

The card colour represents work-order status. Time badges and borders show how long the vehicle has occupied its bay: warnings begin near the bay's limit and escalate after it. **Utilisation** counts occupied bays, including a finished vehicle waiting for collection.

Use **Fullscreen — for a wall display** for a workshop monitor. The board can receive live updates and also supports periodic refresh. Use **Refresh now** if needed.

## What happens next

Releasing a bay frees its floor position. The work order remains available with its existing repair and billing information.

## Related articles

- [Create and manage work orders](/help/en/autoserv-pro/create-and-manage-work-orders)
- [Track technician work](/help/en/autoserv-pro/track-technician-work)

guides.title: Create reusable labour tasks and rates
guides.body:
Labour Tasks is your catalogue of repeatable work, such as an inspection or a component replacement. Advisors can add these tasks to job orders instead of retyping them each time.

## Add a task

1. Open **Workshop → Labour Tasks**.
2. Search the catalogue, then select **Add Labour Task** if the task does not already exist.
3. Enter a unique **Task Code** and a clear **Task Name**.
4. Add a **Description**, **Category**, **Source** and **Type** where useful.
5. Set **Estimated Hours**, **Normal Rate** and **Warranty Rate**. Required rates must be zero or greater.
6. Set **Active** appropriately and select **Save**.

Use names that explain the work to both staff and customers. Estimated hours describe the planned time; they are not evidence that a technician has already performed the task.

## Maintain the catalogue

Use the edit action to change a task's current defaults. Review prices on an existing quote or job separately—do not assume changing the catalogue retrospectively changes earlier documents.

The catalogue also supports managing task categories, sources and types. These organise your choices; keep their meanings consistent across the workshop. Use the import workflow for a prepared spreadsheet of tasks.

## What happens next

The task becomes available to authorised advisors when building job orders and templates. A task added to a job still needs the correct hours, rate, assignment and approval for that visit.

## Troubleshooting

A duplicate **Task Code** prevents creation. If a task is missing from a picker, check its active state and your access. Do not delete a heavily used catalogue entry simply to rename it; use the edit action and review historical reporting implications.

## Related articles

- [Create job templates](/help/en/autoserv-pro/create-job-templates)
- [Import labour tasks and export data](/help/en/autoserv-pro/import-labour-tasks-and-export-data)

guides.title: Create a service package with included parts
guides.body:
A service package bundles a repeatable service and its included items at a package price. Use it for work your workshop routinely sells together.

## Before you begin

Create the required inventory products first. You need permission to manage service packages; seeing estimated cost and margin can require additional cost access.

## Build the package

1. Open **Workshop → Service Packages → Add Service Package**.
2. Enter **Package Name**, choose **Vehicle Type** where applicable, and add a customer-friendly **Description**.
3. Set **Package Price**.
4. Under **Included Parts / Items**, use **Add Item** or **Add first item**.
5. Select each product and review its **Qty**, **Unit Price**, discount and subtotal.
6. Check the items total and any estimated-cost warning. Set the package Active and select **Add Package**.

Use **Update Package** when editing. **Activate** and **Deactivate** control availability without requiring you to remove the package's history.

## Price and cost are different

The package price is what you sell the bundle for. The form's estimated cost helps you assess today's included-parts cost. Actual job profitability depends on the parts consumed and technician time, so the estimate is not a guaranteed margin.

## What happens next

Advisors can add the package to a job order or job template. Review the resulting parts and quantities before saving the job. Do not separately bill an included item a second time unless it represents an additional agreed part outside the package.

## Troubleshooting

If **Cost exceeds price** appears, review the intended package price and item quantities. Hidden cost information means your account lacks access; it does not mean the package has no cost. A stock warning on a job still needs a purchasing or inventory response.

## Related articles

- [Add products and opening stock](/help/en/autoserv-pro/add-products-and-opening-stock)
- [Understand job costs](/help/en/autoserv-pro/understand-job-costs)

guides.title: Save and reuse a job template
guides.body:
A job template combines frequently used labour tasks and service packages. It speeds up preparation while leaving the advisor responsible for the actual vehicle, work and price.

## Create a template

1. Open **Workshop → Job Templates**.
2. Select **Add Template** or **Add First Template**.
3. Enter **Template Name** and an optional description.
4. Under **Labour Tasks**, use **Add Task** and choose the tasks to include.
5. Under **Service Packages**, use **Add Package** and choose the bundles to include.
6. Review **Labour Total**, **Packages Total** and **Estimated Grand Total**, then use **Save Changes**.

You need template-management permission to save changes. Reading and using templates can be granted separately.

## Apply the template to a job

1. Open a new job order and select its work order.
2. Use **Load Template**.
3. In **Load Job Template**, select the required template.
4. Review the appended tasks, packages and resulting included parts.
5. Adjust the work for this vehicle, check quantities and prices, then **Save** the job order.

Loading a template appends its contents. Loading the same one twice can leave duplicate work in the editor, so inspect the line list before saving.

## What happens next

The saved job follows the normal cost approval, technician work, work approval and invoice workflow. Loading a template does not obtain customer agreement or complete the work.

## Troubleshooting

If the template list is empty, create a template or ask someone with access to do so. If its totals look outdated, review the catalogue and template defaults, then verify the actual job lines. Deleting a template cannot be undone through that delete action.

## Related articles

- [Manage labour tasks](/help/en/autoserv-pro/manage-labour-tasks)
- [Create service packages](/help/en/autoserv-pro/create-service-packages)

guides.title: Add inventory products and starting stock
guides.body:
Inventory products represent the parts, fluids and other items your workshop uses or sells. Choose the measurement carefully before the product starts moving through stock.

## Create a product

1. Open **Inventory → Products → Add Product**.
2. In **General**, enter the name, unique code, type and category. Add the brand, supplier and other identifying details where relevant.
3. Choose **Measured in** for the stock unit. For example, a fluid may be counted in litres even if you buy it in cans.
4. Set **Usually bought as** and **Usually used as** if you use packs or smaller consumption units.
5. In **Pricing & Tax**, check the cost, sale price and applicable tax information. Costs and prices must not be negative.
6. In **Stock & Tracking**, set the alert quantity and location. Enter starting quantity only for stock already on your shelf when you first create this product.
7. Complete **Variations** or **Combo Items** only if they apply to the selected product type, then use **Save**.

Opening quantity creates starting stock at the entered cost. Leave it zero if you will receive the same stock through a purchase order; entering both would count the stock twice.

## Maintain the catalogue

Use **Inventory → Categories** and **Brands** to organise products. Use **Edit** and **Update** for product details. After stock movements exist, the stock measurement cannot be changed and quantity is not edited directly on the product form.

## What happens next

The product is available in relevant purchasing and job pickers. Its detail page separates **On hand**, **Available** and **In use**. Check the unit beside each figure before comparing quantities.

## Troubleshooting

Duplicate codes or SKUs prevent saving. A pack or consumption unit from a different measurement family is refused. For a count correction, use Adjustments; for a delivery, receive a purchase. Do not create another product merely to bypass a locked measurement unit without reviewing the existing stock.

## Related articles

- [Units, packs and quantities](/help/en/autoserv-pro/units-packs-and-quantities)
- [Suppliers and purchase orders](/help/en/autoserv-pro/suppliers-and-purchase-orders)

guides.title: Understand units, packs and stock quantities
guides.body:
A unit says how a product is measured. A pack says how much arrives in a container. A job can consume a smaller compatible unit without changing how the workshop values its stock.

## Example: oil bought in cans

Suppose oil is measured in litres and a can contains five litres. Receiving two cans adds ten litres. A job using 200 millilitres consumes 0.2 litres, not 200 litres.

The purchase's **Unit Cost** follows the received container or unit. A job's unit price follows its stock measurement. Always check the conversion shown beside the quantity.

## Set up the measurements

1. Open **Inventory → Units** and review the existing units before adding another.
2. A new unit needs a unique name and code. For a smaller unit, choose its parent and provide the conversion if the system cannot fill in a standard conversion.
3. Open **Inventory → Packs** and define the container, amount and unit. The amount must be greater than zero.
4. On the product, set **Measured in**, **Usually bought as** and **Usually used as**.
5. On a purchase, check **Received as** and the displayed stock quantity. On a job or adjustment, check the selected consumption unit and converted quantity.

## What happens next

Stock movements use the product's measurement. Purchases retain the pack size used when received. Changing a pack already used by purchases retires and replaces it so earlier receipts keep their original meaning.

## Troubleshooting

- A unit from another family cannot be converted: choose compatible volume, weight or count units.
- A product's stock unit is locked once stock movements exist.
- A unit used by products or sub-units cannot simply be deleted.
- A report containing different units should not be interpreted as one physical quantity total.

## Related articles

- [Add products and opening stock](/help/en/autoserv-pro/add-products-and-opening-stock)
- [Adjust and review stock](/help/en/autoserv-pro/adjust-and-review-stock)

guides.title: Add a supplier and receive a purchase order
guides.body:
A purchase order records what you order from a supplier. Stock becomes available through receipt, not merely because you prepared an order.

## Add the supplier

1. Open **Inventory → Suppliers → Add Supplier**.
2. Enter the supplier's contact and company details, phone, email, VAT number and address as appropriate.
3. Select **Save**. Search before adding another record for an existing supplier.

Supplier access and purchase access are separate permissions. Purchase costs may also require cost-viewing access.

## Create the purchase

1. Open **Inventory → Purchase Orders → Add Purchase Order**.
2. Choose **Supplier**, **Order Date**, **Expected Date** and the appropriate **Status**.
3. Under **Line Items**, select **Add Line**.
4. Choose the product, quantity, **Received as**, **Unit Cost** and tax details.
5. Verify the displayed conversion, **Net Total**, **VAT** and **Grand Total** against the supplier document.
6. Save the purchase using the form's save action.

Use Draft or Ordered while preparing or awaiting the order. Set **Received** only when the delivery is actually being recorded. Cancelled orders should not be treated as incoming stock.

## Receive an existing order

Open its edit screen, check the delivered quantities and costs, change **Status** to **Received**, then use **Update**. Check product stock and the purchase afterwards.

## What happens next

Receiving adds the converted quantities to stock and creates the purchase's stock cost records. An unpaid received purchase appears in the supplier-payables workflow. Recording a delivery does not itself prove that the supplier has been paid.

## Troubleshooting

A purchase needs a supplier, date and at least one product line with a positive quantity. If a received order has already supplied parts to jobs, ask the inventory manager before editing or cancelling it: changing it reverses and rebuilds stock records.

## Related articles

- [Transfers and supplier payments](/help/en/autoserv-pro/transfers-and-supplier-payments)
- [Replenish parts for a job](/help/en/autoserv-pro/replenish-parts-for-a-job)

guides.title: Correct stock and investigate its movement
guides.body:
Use an adjustment to record a physical count correction, write-off or other stock change that is not a supplier delivery or repair consumption.

## Record an adjustment

1. Count the affected stock and confirm its measurement unit.
2. Open **Inventory → Adjustments** and start **Add Adjustment**.
3. Choose **Add Stock** or **Remove Stock**.
4. Enter a clear reason in **Notes**.
5. Use **Add Item**, choose the product and enter a positive **Quantity** in the intended unit.
6. Check the converted quantity and select **Save Adjustment**.

The chosen type determines whether stock is added or removed; do not enter a negative quantity to reverse the direction. Each line needs at least 0.001 of its entered unit.

## Review stock history

Open the product and select **Stock history** to examine its changes. For several products over a period, use **Reports → Stock Movement**. Compare references, dates, additions, removals and units with the actual purchase or job.

## What happens next

The adjustment changes stock and adds a movement record. Stock added through an adjustment also becomes available for later consumption. It does not create a supplier purchase or supplier payment.

## Troubleshooting

If a count looks wrong, check whether an estimate or job already allocated the parts, whether the purchase was received twice, and whether the quantity was entered as packs or stock units. A second unexplained adjustment hides the cause rather than resolving it.

Do not use an adjustment to cancel a customer's financial charge. Review stock and billing through their own records. Deleting or reversing existing stock movements should be handled by an authorised inventory manager.

## Related articles

- [Units, packs and quantities](/help/en/autoserv-pro/units-packs-and-quantities)
- [Request and issue parts](/help/en/autoserv-pro/request-and-issue-parts)

guides.title: Request parts and track the storekeeper's response
guides.body:
Parts Requests coordinates what technicians need and what the storekeeper has supplied. A request is not the same as a received purchase or an invoice line.

## Request parts as a technician

1. Open **My Work → My Dashboard** and use **Request Parts** for the relevant work.
2. Select each product and enter **Qty**. Use **Add part** for additional items.
3. Add useful notes, including the job context where needed.
4. Use **Submit Request**.
5. Follow the request through **My Work → Parts Requests**.

## Handle the request as a storekeeper

1. Open **Inventory → Parts Requests** and find the request.
2. Check the job, requested quantities and available stock.
3. Use **Approve** only when available stock covers the request.
4. Use **Mark Ordered** when purchasing is needed, or **Reject** with the appropriate explanation when the request should not proceed.
5. Use **Mark Issued** when you actually hand over the parts.
6. Have the technician acknowledge receipt through their request screen where available.

Approval can be blocked by insufficient available stock even when a product appears in the catalogue. Check the available figure, not only the product's name or its last purchased quantity.

## What happens next

The request records its progress and issue details. Staff still need to ensure the job contains the correct parts and quantities for stock and billing. Do not add the same physical part twice just because it appears in both a request and a job.

## Troubleshooting

A rejected request needs a new request if the parts are still required. If stock is short, receive the actual delivery before trying to approve again. Changing the request to Ordered does not create or receive a purchase order by itself.

## Related articles

- [Suppliers and purchase orders](/help/en/autoserv-pro/suppliers-and-purchase-orders)
- [Replenish parts for a job](/help/en/autoserv-pro/replenish-parts-for-a-job)

guides.title: Create, review and issue an invoice
guides.body:
An invoice bills the work completed for a customer. Drafting, approving, issuing and taking payment are separate actions with separate permissions.

## Before you begin

Check that the job order's work is approved and that it has not already been invoiced. Have the correct customer, agreed prices, tax treatment and any advance payments ready for review.

## Prepare the invoice

1. Use **Add Invoice** from the approved job, or open **Operations → Invoices → Add Invoice**.
2. Select the customer and the eligible **Job Orders** entry.
3. Check **Invoice Date** and **Due Date**. The final **Invoice No.** is assigned at issue.
4. Review **Labour Tasks**, **Service Packages** and **Products / Parts**, including hours, quantities, rates and discounts.
5. Under **Adjustments & Notes**, check **Order Discount (%)**, tax, shipping and notes.
6. Review **Total Summary**, including **Advance Applied** and the remaining amount to collect.
7. Use **Save as Draft** if the document needs further review.

The order discount applies across parts, labour and packages, not shipping. Check each product's tax as well as the fallback rate; a displayed UAE default is not automatically correct for every workshop or transaction.

## Issue the checked invoice

Open the draft. An authorised reviewer can use **Approve**. When the document is final, an authorised issuer uses **Issue** and accepts the lock warning. Invoice approval is available as a separate review stage; the issue action can also operate on a draft.

## What happens next

Issuing assigns the permanent number, applies eligible work-order advances, and locks the job order and invoice lines. A draft or approved invoice is not yet the final issued document. Payments can be recorded only after issue.

**Collect Payment** on creation is optional. Use **Save & Record Payment** only for money actually received and check both the saved invoice and payment result afterwards.

## Troubleshooting

If no job is selectable, check work approval, customer selection and whether it was already billed. If issuance succeeds but payment fails, open the existing invoice and record the payment there; do not create another invoice.

## Related articles

- [Record invoice payments](/help/en/autoserv-pro/record-invoice-payments)
- [Invoice and payment problems](/help/en/autoserv-pro/invoice-and-payment-problems)

guides.title: Record a full or partial invoice payment
guides.body:
Use invoice payments for money received against an issued invoice. Creating or issuing the invoice does not mean that the customer has paid it.

## Record a payment

1. Open **Operations → Invoices** and find the issued invoice.
2. Review **Total**, **Paid**, any applied advance and **Balance Due**.
3. Use **Record Payment**.
4. Select **Payment Method**, enter the **Amount**, **Payment Date** and useful **Notes**.
5. Check the displayed remaining balance and submit using **Record Payment**.
6. Reopen the invoice and confirm the entry under **Payments Received**.

The amount must be at least 0.01 and must not exceed the balance due. Enter only the amount actually received. A partial payment leaves the unpaid remainder on the invoice.

## Choose the correct method

The normal payment dialog offers methods such as **Cash**, **Card**, **Bank Transfer**, **Cheque**, **Online Payment** and **Other**. Recording a card or online method manually does not charge a card or contact a payment provider.

Where enabled, **Pay Online** opens the configured online-payment route. Check the invoice after the provider confirms payment before entering any manual receipt for the same money.

Gift-card payment controls are available in the invoice creation flow, not the later **Record Payment** dialog. Check the card's code, expiry and available balance. Do not treat a gift-card redemption as new cash received.

## What happens next

The invoice's paid amount and remaining balance update. A payment-confirmation email may be queued when email is configured; successful recording and successful delivery are different outcomes.

## Troubleshooting

Draft and approved invoices cannot accept payment. If the amount appears too high, check advances and earlier payments first. After a timeout, reload **Payments Received** before retrying. Ask the billing administrator to handle an incorrect receipt; do not record another positive payment to cancel it.

## Related articles

- [Advances and bulk payments](/help/en/autoserv-pro/advances-and-bulk-payments)
- [Payment accounts and ledger](/help/en/autoserv-pro/payment-accounts-and-ledger)

guides.title: Record a work-order advance or a bulk payment
guides.body:
An advance records money received before the invoice is issued. A bulk payment distributes one receipt across several outstanding invoices. Both require payment permission.

## Record an advance

1. Open the relevant work order before it has been invoiced.
2. In **Advance Payment**, enter **Amount**, **Method**, **Account**, **Date** and **Note**.
3. Select **Record Advance**.
4. Check **Advances on this work order** to confirm the amount was recorded once.

When an invoice for that visit is issued, eligible unapplied advances are attached to it. Check **Advance Applied** and the remaining balance before collecting more money. Do not record the same advance again as an invoice payment.

The advance's **Void** action reverses its recorded effect and cannot be undone through the same action. An advance already applied to an invoice cannot be voided as an unattached advance; ask the billing administrator to review it.

## Record one payment across invoices

1. Open **Invoices → Bulk Payment** and select the customer, or use the available bulk-payment action from the relevant account.
2. Enter the total amount received, method, account, date and note.
3. Review the allocation preview. Automatic allocation starts with the oldest due invoices; invoices without a due date follow dated ones.
4. Adjust the allocations if needed. Each allocation must fit that invoice's balance and the allocations must match the receipt.
5. Submit the payment and check the affected invoices.

## What happens next

Each invoice receives its allocated portion. Bulk payment is not a way to mix different customers' receipts or put an unexplained excess into an account.

Customer **Deposits** are a separate feature from work-order advances. Their balance display and redemption path require administrator review; do not substitute a deposit entry for this advance workflow.

## Troubleshooting

If no open invoices appear, check the customer and issue status. If the allocation does not match, correct it before submitting. After a slow response, reload the payment records before trying again.

## Related articles

- [Record invoice payments](/help/en/autoserv-pro/record-invoice-payments)
- [Fleet billing and payments](/help/en/autoserv-pro/fleet-billing-and-payments)

guides.title: Print a job card, invoice or payment receipt
guides.body:
Use the document preview to check what the customer or workshop will receive. A printout reflects a record; it does not perform an approval or payment.

## Print a document

1. Open the work order and use **Print job card**, or open an invoice and use **Print**.
2. Review the preview and select an available document template. Extra layouts depend on your plan.
3. Check the language, customer, vehicle, lines, totals and any bank details.
4. Adjust the available print options, then use **Print**.
5. In your browser's print dialog, choose a printer or save to PDF.

The preview can switch between English and Arabic. The workshop default template provides the starting point, while your browser may remember your last-used selection for that document type.

## Print a receipt or share an invoice

In an invoice's **Payments Received** area, use **Print receipt** for the relevant payment. Check that the receipt matches the actual amount and date.

Where the invoice print preview offers sharing, generate the link and read its expiry date. Copy or share the link using the offered controls. Sending a link requires invoice-send permission.

Anyone holding the public document link can open it. Confirm the recipient before sending a financial document, and avoid public or unrelated group conversations.

## What happens next

The customer can open the shared document without a staff login until the link expires. A draft preview is a provisional document; the official invoice number is assigned only when the invoice is issued.

## Troubleshooting

If the preview is blank, wait for it to load and try reopening it before printing. If the generated PDF is still blank or incomplete, contact support with the document reference and selected template. An expired link needs a fresh share link. Do not delete the original invoice to fix a print problem.

## Related articles

- [Company branding and preferences](/help/en/autoserv-pro/company-branding-and-preferences)
- [Email, WhatsApp and link problems](/help/en/autoserv-pro/email-whatsapp-and-link-problems)

guides.title: Set up payment accounts and review the ledger
guides.body:
Payment accounts identify where workshop money is held. The ledger shows recorded money moving in and out. Reading finance and changing accounts require different permissions.

## Add a payment account

1. Open **Finance → Accounts → Add account**.
2. Enter **Account name**, choose **Type**, and add a **Reference** or **Details** if useful.
3. Enter the account's actual **Opening balance** for your agreed starting point.
4. Keep **Active** selected for an account in use.
5. Use **Default for type** only if payments of that type should normally be directed to this account.
6. Click **Save**.

Account names must be unique. An opening balance is a starting balance, not a new sale, customer deposit or expense. Have the person responsible for the books confirm it before regular posting begins.

## Review money movements

1. Open **Finance → Ledger**.
2. Choose the date range, account, direction and method filters you need.
3. Compare **Money in**, **Money out**, **Net** and **Balance at end**.
4. Use the movement's source/reference to investigate the original receipt, expense or transfer.

The ledger can include reversals. Read the direction and reversal label rather than treating every row as new money received.

## What happens next

New receipts and payments use the selected account or the relevant default. Changing an account default is a setting for subsequent recording, not a reason to assume old movements have moved accounts.

## Troubleshooting

An account with ledger entries cannot simply be deleted; deactivate it when it should no longer be used. If a balance looks wrong, compare the opening balance and dated movements with your external records. Do not add an unrelated income entry merely to make the balance match.

## Related articles

- [Expenses and other income](/help/en/autoserv-pro/expenses-and-other-income)
- [Transfers and supplier payments](/help/en/autoserv-pro/transfers-and-supplier-payments)

guides.title: Record expenses and income outside invoices
guides.body:
Use **Expenses** for workshop costs such as rent, utilities, salaries or subcontracted work. Use **Income** for receipts that are not customer invoice payments, such as a scrap sale.

## Record an expense

1. Open **Finance → Expenses → Record expense**.
2. Enter **Date**, **Amount (incl. VAT)**, **Of which VAT** and **Category**.
3. Choose a supplier or enter a **Vendor** where appropriate.
4. Select **Paid now** for money already paid, or **Pay later (pending)** for a bill still awaiting payment.
5. Check **Payment method**, **Paid from**, due date and details, then **Save**.
6. Use **Upload receipt** on the saved expense if you have a supporting document.

The VAT field is part of the amount, not an extra charge added on top. It must not exceed the total amount. Receipt uploads accept JPG, PNG, WebP or PDF up to 8 MB.

## Pay a pending expense

Use **Mark paid** and enter the actual payment details. A pending bill is recorded as a cost but should not be confused with cash that has already left the account.

Payroll categories can offer employee details. Viewing or recording pay-related amounts requires employee-compensation access. Hidden payroll figures are withheld, not zero.

## Record other income

Open **Finance → Income → Record income**, enter the date, inclusive amount, VAT portion, category and payer, then choose the method and **Received into** account and **Save**.

## What happens next

Paid expenses and received income create their corresponding money movements. Posted amount, account, method and date are locked. An authorised person must **Void** and re-record when those financial facts are wrong.

## Troubleshooting

Do not record an invoice payment again under Income: it would duplicate the receipt. Do not record a supplier payment again as a new expense if the purchase already represents the cost. A void is a reversal, not a delete-and-forget action.

## Related articles

- [Payment accounts and ledger](/help/en/autoserv-pro/payment-accounts-and-ledger)
- [Financial reports and statements](/help/en/autoserv-pro/financial-reports-and-statements)

guides.title: Transfer money and settle supplier purchases
guides.body:
Use Transfers when money moves between workshop accounts. Use Payables when money settles a supplier's purchase. These actions have separate permissions from simply recording an expense.

## Record a transfer

1. Open **Finance → Transfers → Add transfer**.
2. Choose **Type**: an account transfer, owner deposit or owner withdrawal as appropriate.
3. Select **From account** and **To account** as required by that type.
4. Enter the positive **Amount**, actual **Date**, reference and note.
5. Click **Save** and check both accounts in the ledger.

A transfer must use different source and destination accounts. Banking workshop cash is a transfer, not another sale. An owner deposit is different from a customer's advance payment.

## Record a supplier payment

1. Open **Finance → Payables**.
2. Find the received purchase with a balance and select **Record Payment**.
3. Verify **Supplier**, **Purchase** and the balance due.
4. Enter **Amount**, **Date**, **Method**, **Account**, reference and notes.
5. Submit and confirm that the purchase balance decreases by the intended amount.

The purchase must belong to the selected supplier. Payments must be at least 0.01 and cannot exceed the balance due.

## What happens next

A transfer records the corresponding account movements. A supplier payment settles part or all of the outstanding purchase. A pending or ordered purchase is not treated like a received purchase in the Payables list.

## Correct a mistake

An authorised user can **Void** a transfer; both of its recorded sides are reversed. Supplier-payment reversal also requires separate reversal permission. Review the original record before using either action, and do not record a second outgoing payment as a correction.

## Related articles

- [Suppliers and purchase orders](/help/en/autoserv-pro/suppliers-and-purchase-orders)
- [Payment accounts and ledger](/help/en/autoserv-pro/payment-accounts-and-ledger)

guides.title: Understand parts, labour and subcontracted job costs
guides.body:
Job costing helps managers compare what a job earns with what it costs the workshop. A selling price is not the same as a cost, and an estimated cost may differ from the final result.

## Review a job's cost

1. Open the relevant job order and review the available costing summary.
2. Check the parts quantities and whether any are backordered.
3. Review technician time and the labour-cost basis with an authorised manager.
4. Check any additional cost lines and compare the result with the relevant profitability report.

Parts cost can use the purchase stock allocated to the job. A shortfall may be valued using an estimate, so a saved job is not proof that its entire cost is final. Package costing includes its consumed parts and recorded work.

Labour cost can be derived from an employee's salary and working-time settings or their hourly cost override. Staff without employee-pay access may see parts cost while labour cost, overall cost and margin remain withheld.

## Record subcontracted or internal costs

Where your plan and permissions expose job cost lines, select the appropriate kind and enter its description and cost. A subcontracted **Sublet** line requires either the supplier or a vendor name, not both, and can include a customer selling price and paid/pending status.

A sublet can create a linked expense. Check for that linked record before entering another expense manually. An internal cost line is for internal job tracking; it does not itself create an expense or account movement.

## What happens next

Cost information supports pricing and management review. It does not automatically collect money or prove that every reported margin includes every business expense.

## Troubleshooting

If a linked sublet expense is already posted, its cost or vendor cannot simply be changed; the authorised finance user must review the void-and-correct process. If cost information is hidden, request the appropriate access rather than replacing it with guessed values.

## Related articles

- [Add employees and share access](/help/en/autoserv-pro/add-employees-and-share-access)
- [Financial reports and statements](/help/en/autoserv-pro/financial-reports-and-statements)

guides.title: Manage a fleet account and its drivers
guides.body:
A fleet account groups a business customer's vehicles, drivers and billing activity. Fleet viewing, management and financial access can be granted separately, and the feature depends on your plan.

## Create the account

1. Open **Workshop → Fleet → Add Fleet Account**.
2. Select the customer and enter **Company Name**.
3. Choose **Billing Cycle**, add notes and check **Active**.
4. Click **Save** and open the new account.

## Add a driver and vehicle assignment

1. Open the account's **Drivers** tab and select **Add Driver**.
2. Enter **Driver Name**, phone and **Assigned Vehicle**.
3. Complete the relevant driving-licence, Emirates ID, ITC permit and medical-expiry details when your workshop needs to track them.
4. Check the dates and active state, then **Save**.
5. Review the **Vehicles** tab to confirm the expected vehicle association.

These fields record information; they do not verify a document with an issuing authority. Keep access to identity information limited to the people who need it.

## Review the fleet

Use **Vehicles** for vehicle and PM information, **Work Orders** for workshop visits, and **Billing** for financial activity if you have access. A **Rate Card** can hold a labour-rate override and parts discount. Review the actual job and invoice values before relying on the account default.

## What happens next

The account gives your workshop a shared view of that fleet's activity. Adding a driver or changing a rate card does not create repair work, complete maintenance or collect payment.

## Troubleshooting

If a vehicle is missing, check the driver/vehicle association and customer record. If Billing is hidden, ask for the appropriate fleet-financial access. Removing a driver removes the fleet association; do not use it to erase vehicle service or payment history.

## Related articles

- [Fleet billing and payments](/help/en/autoserv-pro/fleet-billing-and-payments)
- [Maintenance and driver handovers](/help/en/autoserv-pro/maintenance-and-driver-handovers)

guides.title: Prepare a fleet bill and record payment
guides.body:
Fleet billing consolidates eligible workshop invoice activity for a fleet account over a selected period. It is connected to the underlying workshop invoices; it is not another unrelated sale.

## Prepare the billing period

1. Open **Workshop → Fleet**, select the account and open **Billing**.
2. Select **Generate Fleet Invoice**.
3. Enter **Period Start**, **Period End**, **PO Reference**, **Credit Days** and notes as appropriate.
4. Select **Preview billable jobs**.
5. Compare the listed vehicles, work orders, amounts and tax with the underlying workshop records.
6. Use **Generate Invoice** only once the preview is correct.

The end date cannot precede the start date. The available credit terms are 15, 30, 45 or 60 days. Check the displayed due date on the saved bill; it is calculated from the billing period end in this workflow.

## Record a fleet receipt

1. Open the fleet invoice using **View**.
2. Review its balance and **Payments Received**.
3. Use **Record Payment**, enter the actual amount, method, date and reference, then submit.
4. Check the new payment and remaining balance. Use **Bulk Payment** from the account when one receipt covers several fleet invoices.

Amounts must be positive and cannot exceed the relevant balance. Do not separately record the same money on each underlying workshop invoice after using fleet settlement without checking its allocation.

## What happens next

The consolidated document and its payment history remain available from the account. **PDF** provides a downloadable document. A paid state should be supported by recorded payment, not only a manual status change.

## Troubleshooting

If the preview is empty, check the account, period and whether the work was already included. Where **Reverse** is available, it requires separate permission and a reason; review linked or bulk-payment information before confirming. Check both fleet and underlying balances after any correction.

## Related articles

- [Advances and bulk payments](/help/en/autoserv-pro/advances-and-bulk-payments)
- [Financial reports and statements](/help/en/autoserv-pro/financial-reports-and-statements)

guides.title: Review preventive maintenance and record a driver handover
guides.body:
The **PM Board** tracks configured mileage-based maintenance schedules. Driver handovers record a vehicle's condition and odometer at a shift change. These are different from a customer repair invoice.

## Review maintenance

1. Open **Workshop → PM Board**.
2. Use **All**, **Overdue**, **Due Soon** or **Upcoming**, and search by plate or service.
3. Compare **Due at**, **Now at** and the last recorded service.
4. After the service has actually been completed, use **Mark Done**, enter the completion mileage and confirm.

Completion updates the last-service information and calculates the next due mileage from the interval. A higher completion reading can update the vehicle's odometer.

The **Add WO** option is part of this completion flow and can also create a work order. Do not use it merely to plan future work if the service has not been done. For an empty PM Board, ask the administrator to confirm schedule setup; the available schedule-editor entry point may differ by deployment.

## Record a driver handover

1. Open the workshop's provided driver-handover page.
2. Look up the plate and confirm the vehicle shown.
3. Enter **Handed By**, **Received By** and **Odometer Reading (km)**.
4. Record **Fuel Level**, or **Battery Level (%)** where appropriate, plus **Vehicle Condition** and any damage notes.
5. Review carefully and use **Submit Handover**.

The handover form is a public form, not a staff-authenticated identity check. Use the correct vehicle and actual reading. The form refuses a reading lower than the last displayed odometer.

## What happens next
