The handover is saved, a higher reading updates mileage, and PM alerts can appear. The workshop notification is a courtesy; urgent damage or safety concerns should also be reported directly to the workshop.

## Related articles

- [Fleet accounts and drivers](/help/en/autoserv-pro/fleet-accounts-and-drivers)
- [Add and manage vehicles](/help/en/autoserv-pro/add-and-manage-vehicles)

guides.title: Record an insurance policy and follow a claim
guides.body:
Insurance Claims connects a policy and claim to a vehicle and customer. Filing or updating operational claim details is separate from approving settlement figures.

## Add the record

1. Open **Workshop → Insurance Claims → Add Insurance Record**.
2. Select the vehicle and confirm the customer that fills in.
3. Review **Prior Claims** where available.
4. Enter **Insurance Company**, **Policy No.**, **Expiry Date** and the insurer phone number.
5. Add **Claim No.** if assigned and choose the relevant **Repair Type**.
6. Select **Add Record**.

Vehicle, customer, insurer, policy number and expiry date are required. **Agency Repair** and **Non-Agency Repair** describe the repair arrangement; selecting them does not establish insurer acceptance.

## Follow the claim

1. Open **View** to inspect **Claim Detail**.
2. Use the available status action for Pending, Submitted or Surveyor Assigned as the case progresses.
3. Record **Surveyor Name**, **Surveyor Phone**, visit date and the relevant note, then use **Save Details**.
4. An authorised settlement user can record assessed/approved amounts, customer excess and Approved, Rejected or Paid status.
5. Use **Raise Supplementary Claim** only for genuine additional costs that need a linked claim.

## What happens next

Claim information remains connected to the vehicle, and work orders marked **Insurance Claim** can carry policy coverage details. **Insurance Receivables Aging** helps review outstanding approved claims.

A claim marked Paid is a claim-workflow fact. Confirm the actual money receipt through your workshop's billing and finance records; do not assume changing the claim status records every required payment entry.

## Troubleshooting

If settlement controls are unavailable, check insurance-settlement permission. If a selected vehicle fills in the wrong customer, correct the vehicle/customer association before filing the claim. Review supplementary claims carefully to avoid counting the original amount twice.

## Related articles

- [Create and manage work orders](/help/en/autoserv-pro/create-and-manage-work-orders)
- [Roles and permissions](/help/en/autoserv-pro/roles-and-permissions)

guides.title: Add an employee and send their login link
guides.body:
An employee record links a staff login with workshop information such as role, department and technician costing. Employee-management, access-link and compensation permissions are separate.

## Add the employee

1. Open **Configuration → Employees → Add Employee**.
2. Enter **Name**, **Email** and **Username**. Email and username must be unique.
3. Add **Phone**, **Department**, **Job Title** and **Hire Date** as appropriate.
4. Select **Role**. A technician must have the **Technician** role; typing Technician as a job title alone is not enough.
5. Leave **Password** blank if the employee should choose their own using the access link.
6. If authorised, enter **Basic Salary**, **Working Days / Month**, **Working Hours / Day** and an optional **Hourly Cost Rate**.
7. Click **Save**.

Working days must be between 1 and 31, and working hours between 1 and 24. The hourly cost override must not be negative. Without an override, the costing basis can be derived from salary divided by the configured working days and hours.

## Share access

Use the **Share access** panel after creation or **Login link** on the employee row. Choose **Copy message**, **Send by email** or **Send on WhatsApp**. Check whether WhatsApp actually sent through the connected provider or opened a message for you to send manually.

The link lets the employee set their own password. It works once and expires in 48 hours. **Renew link (the old one stops working)** replaces an expired or unsuitable link.

## What happens next

The employee signs in with their own account and sees the permitted screens. A technician becomes assignable when their employee record and Technician-role login are correctly linked.

## Troubleshooting

If the email or username is already used, inspect the existing staff account before creating another. If salary controls are hidden, ask the compensation administrator. Keep access links private; do not post one in a shared workshop group.

## Related articles

- [Sign in and passwords](/help/en/autoserv-pro/sign-in-and-passwords)
- [Roles and permissions](/help/en/autoserv-pro/roles-and-permissions)

guides.title: Set your workshop details, branding and preferences
guides.body:
Company Settings controls the workshop identity and common display preferences. Viewing settings and saving changes require different permissions.

## Update the workshop

1. Open **Configuration → Company Settings**.
2. Under **Company Information**, check **Business / App Name**, **Short Name**, legal company name, TRN, country, contact details and address.
3. Under **Branding & Logos**, use **Upload image** for your workshop branding and choose **Brand colour**.
4. Under **Regional & Format**, check language, date format, currency, decimal places and timezone.
5. Under **Printing**, choose the available default invoice template and enter bank details only if they should appear on documents.
6. Review **Interface Preferences**, including theme, default rows per page and confirmation style.
7. Use **Save Changes** and wait for the saved confirmation before leaving.

The brand colour is used on customer-facing booking, tracking, inspection and estimate pages. Extra document templates can depend on your plan. A user's device may remember a different last-used print template.

## Customer portal

The **Customer Self-Service Portal** section provides the **Portal Login URL** and **Open Portal**. Customer access still needs the customer's email and portal password; displaying the portal URL does not create those credentials.

## Download a backup

Authorised users can use **Download a backup** under **Admin Actions**. The downloaded ZIP contains workshop records and uploaded files, including readable customer and financial information. Save it in a location controlled by the business. Downloading it does not restore or alter the workshop.

## Troubleshooting

Review an example document after changing branding or bank details. Changing the currency setting is not an exchange-rate conversion of historical transactions. If you have unsaved changes, save or deliberately discard them before navigating away.

## Related articles

- [Configure document numbering](/help/en/autoserv-pro/configure-document-numbering)
- [Print and share documents](/help/en/autoserv-pro/print-and-share-documents)
- [Customer portal](/help/en/autoserv-pro/customer-portal)

guides.title: Configure inspection templates and checkpoints
guides.body:
Inspection templates define what technicians check. Different templates can suit a quick service check and a detailed paid inspection.

## Create or edit a template

1. Open **Configuration → Inspection Templates**.
2. Select **Add template**, or use **Edit** on an existing one.
3. Enter **Name** and **Description**.
4. Use **Add section** to group related checks.
5. Use **Add checkpoint** within each section. Define the check and any supported reading, unit or threshold details.
6. Select **Default template** if this should be the starting choice for new inspections.
7. Review the order and wording, then select **Save**.

The template needs a name and at least one useful checkpoint. Keep wording specific enough that two technicians understand the same check in the same way. A suggested verdict based on a reading still needs professional review.

## Change a template safely

Editing creates a new template version. Existing inspections retain the version and recorded findings associated with them; changing a template is not a way to correct an already completed inspection.

A template that has been used for an inspection cannot be deleted. Deactivate it instead when it should no longer be offered for new work.

## What happens next

Technicians choose the appropriate checklist when using **Start inspection** on a work order. The configured default is offered for new inspections. Completed findings can be shared and flagged items can become an estimate.

## Troubleshooting

If technicians see “No inspection template is set up yet,” check that there is an active default. If a new checkpoint does not appear in an older inspection, start a new inspection rather than expecting the historical record to change.

## Related articles

- [Inspect a vehicle](/help/en/autoserv-pro/inspect-a-vehicle)
- [Inspection to approved repair](/help/en/autoserv-pro/inspection-to-approved-repair)

guides.title: Configure document numbering
guides.body:
Document Numbering controls the prefixes and sequences used for new workshop documents. Only authorised settings managers should change it.

## Review a document series

1. Open **Configuration → Numbering**.
2. Find the required **Document** row.
3. Review **Prefix**, **Digits**, **Next No.** and the **Next number** preview.
4. Change only the values agreed for that series.
5. Set **Reset yearly** where appropriate and use **Save**.

The prefix accepts letters and numbers up to ten characters. Padding must be between three and six digits. The next number must be a positive whole number. The system can refuse a value that would reuse an already issued number.

## Understand when numbers are assigned

Work orders receive their numbers when created. Job orders can inherit the work-order sequence, with their own counter as a fallback. Invoices use a temporary draft reference until **Issue** assigns the final invoice number.

Changing a series affects future numbering. It does not rename issued invoices or make a draft an issued document.

## What happens next

Check the next-number preview after saving and verify the next legitimate document created by the business. There is no need to issue a dummy invoice just to check a prefix.

## Troubleshooting

If a counter change is refused, review the existing documents with your administrator. Do not lower a counter or delete documents to force a preferred number. If numbering looks unexpected, distinguish the draft reference, work-order lineage and final issued invoice number first.

## Related articles

- [Create and issue an invoice](/help/en/autoserv-pro/create-and-issue-an-invoice)
- [Company branding and preferences](/help/en/autoserv-pro/company-branding-and-preferences)

guides.title: Connect workshop email and review message templates
guides.body:
Email Settings separates the sending connection from the wording of messages. Configuring the sender requires messaging-configuration access; editing templates requires email-template management access.

## Connect an email account

1. Open **Configuration → Email Settings → Mail Driver**.
2. Select **Add Mail Driver** and choose the supported sending method used by your provider.
3. Enter the requested provider details. For a mail-server connection, these include **Host**, **Port**, **Username**, password and the offered encryption setting.
4. Enter **From Address** and **From Name**. Use an address your provider permits you to send from.
5. Save the connection.
6. For an SMTP connection, use **Check connection**. This checks connectivity and sign-in without sending an email.
7. Use **Send test email** with an address you control and verify receipt.
8. Use **Activate** when the tested connection should be used for workshop email.

Saved passwords and provider keys are shown as configured, not revealed in full. Leave them unchanged when editing unrelated fields. Use the explicit clearing controls only when you intend to remove a saved secret.

## Review templates and delivery

Open **Templates**, choose the relevant message, and review its subject, content and preview. Keep the supplied placeholders intact so customer and document details can be inserted. The **Layout** tab controls shared email presentation; its editor is advanced, so ask your administrator for help if you are not familiar with the format.

Use a test email after changes. Open **Send Logs** and filter by recipient, template or status to investigate sending problems.

## What happens next

Eligible workshop events use the active sending connection and enabled templates. A record can save even if its email later fails, so do not repeat the business transaction merely to resend a notification.

## Troubleshooting

Check sender permission, credentials, host, port and provider restrictions. Connection success does not guarantee inbox placement: inspect the recipient's spam folder and the send log. Never include passwords or provider keys in a support screenshot.

## Related articles

- [Messaging and campaigns](/help/en/autoserv-pro/messaging-and-campaigns)
- [Email, WhatsApp and link problems](/help/en/autoserv-pro/email-whatsapp-and-link-problems)

guides.title: Connect WhatsApp or SMS and send a campaign
guides.body:
Messaging Settings connects the workshop to a supported message provider. Announcements prepares campaigns for a selected audience. A WhatsApp Business app installed on a phone is not, by itself, a configured SAM messaging connection.

## Connect a provider

1. Open **Configuration → Messaging Settings**.
2. Select **WhatsApp** or **SMS** and use **Add WhatsApp Account** or **Add SMS Account**.
3. Choose the provider and enter the fields requested for that provider.
4. Check the sending number, account label and any country or message-template settings shown.
5. Save the configuration and use its test-send action with a number you control.
6. Read the result, verify receipt and activate the account when ready.

The screen supports WhatsApp providers such as Meta, Twilio and 360dialog, and SMS provider choices including Twilio, Vonage, ClickSend and a custom gateway. Use the values from the provider account approved for your workshop. Test sends are real messages and may be charged by the provider.

## Send an announcement campaign

1. Open **Workshop → Announcements → Add Campaign**.
2. Enter **Campaign Title**, **Email Subject** where relevant, and **Message**.
3. Choose **Channel** and **Target Audience**.
4. Check the recipient preview and **Save** the draft.
5. Review the saved campaign, then use **Send Campaign** only when the audience and content are correct.

Preparing a campaign and sending it require separate permissions. The plan must also allow the feature. Only draft campaigns can be sent.

## What happens next

The campaign is queued for recipients with a usable contact method. The actual count can differ from the audience preview if some recipients lack the selected channel. Queued or sent-to-provider is not proof that every customer read it.

## Troubleshooting

If no recipients match, check the audience and channel. If a tracking or approval action only copies a link, send that link manually in the existing customer conversation. Check provider settings rather than repeatedly sending the same campaign.

## Related articles

- [Share progress and inspections](/help/en/autoserv-pro/share-progress-and-inspections)
- [Email settings and templates](/help/en/autoserv-pro/email-settings-and-templates)

guides.title: Review your plan, trial and subscription payments
guides.body:
The hosted edition provides **Plan & Billing** for workshop subscription information. This subscription is different from the invoices your workshop sends to vehicle owners. Standalone installations do not use the same hosted billing screens.

## Review the current plan

1. Open **Configuration → Plan & Billing**.
2. Check the current plan, trial end date if applicable, and usage meters.
3. Review the available plan choices and billing cycle.
4. Read the amount and terms shown in the current checkout before proceeding. Selecting a plan card alone does not complete a purchase.

Only an authorised settings manager should purchase or activate a plan. Available features and limits depend on the workshop's actual subscription, so use the current account information rather than an old price or feature list.

## Trial expiry and extension

An expired trial can leave records readable while blocking new changes. Eligible workshops can request the offered self-service extension during the last week of the trial or after expiry. The extension is available once; check the new end date shown after it succeeds.

If the extension is unavailable or already used, contact the product team through the offered support route. Do not delete useful business records merely to work around a limit.

## Review payment history

Use **Subscription & payments** to review available subscription history and **Download invoice** for its documents. **Manage on Orions360** opens the connected subscription management route where provided.

## What happens next

After successful checkout and activation, refresh the plan information and check the resulting entitlement. A cancelled or failed checkout is not a successful upgrade.

## Troubleshooting

If the provider confirms payment but the plan has not changed, keep the payment reference and contact support before paying again. A missing feature can also be a staff-permission issue. Account suspension needs support assistance; a password reset will not remove it.

## Related articles

- [Login, access and plan problems](/help/en/autoserv-pro/login-access-and-plan-problems)
- [Use Sami](/help/en/autoserv-pro/use-sami)

guides.title: Ask Sami about your workshop
guides.body:
Sami is the workshop assistant. It can answer supported operational and business questions using the information your account is permitted to access, and prepare certain actions for your confirmation.

## Ask a useful question

1. Select **Ask Sami**.
2. Enter one clear question, including the date range, customer or job reference when relevant.
3. Review the answer and compare important figures with the linked record or report before acting on them.
4. Ask a narrower follow-up if the question was too broad.

Useful examples include “Which jobs are overdue?”, “What is occupying the bays?” or “What payments were received this week?” The supported tools also cover areas such as outstanding receivables, technician activity and selected financial summaries. Access to a report through Sami still requires its permissions.

## Review an action draft

Sami can prepare supported work-order or payment actions as a draft card. Review every field, including customer, vehicle, job or invoice, amount and date. Use the card's confirmation action only when it matches what you intend. Discard it if it is wrong.

A draft is not a completed transaction. After confirmation, check the actual record before asking Sami to repeat the action. If the draft has expired or is no longer available, review the current record and prepare a fresh one if still needed.

## What happens next

Confirmed actions pass through the same product permissions and business checks as the corresponding manual action. A user who cannot record a payment does not gain that ability by asking the assistant.

## Troubleshooting

The assistant requires access and a plan that includes it. Trial allowances and rate limits can restrict questions; read the message shown rather than assuming all plans are unlimited. Keep each message within 2,000 characters. Do not paste passwords, provider keys or unrelated personal information into a question.

If your workshop has a configured Telegram connection, ask the administrator for its approved setup route. No Telegram account is connected merely by opening Sami in the browser.

## Related articles

- [Roles and permissions](/help/en/autoserv-pro/roles-and-permissions)
- [Workshop and sales reports](/help/en/autoserv-pro/workshop-and-sales-reports)

guides.title: Choose the right workshop or sales report
guides.body:
Start with the question you want to answer. Reports use different records and dates, so two legitimate reports can show different totals.

## Run a report

1. Open **Reports → All Reports** or choose the specific report in the sidebar.
2. Select the period and any employee, customer, product or grouping filters provided.
3. Review the report's notes and missing-data labels before interpreting the result.
4. Use the offered export format if you need to share the same filtered report.

- **Daily Job Card** — What to use it for: Work listed by job date, vehicle, status and assigned people. What to watch: The separate parts total does not include parts bundled inside packages.
- **Mechanic Efficiency** — What to use it for: Technician time and performance. What to watch: Check available working hours and the selected period.
- **Labour Revenue** — What to use it for: Labour contribution by employee or department. What to watch: Shared work is apportioned; missing assignments are disclosed.
- **Service-wise** — What to use it for: Use and value of labour tasks and packages. What to watch: Based on job activity, not cash receipts.
- **Acquisition Source** — What to use it for: New customers grouped by how they found the workshop. What to watch: Historical missing sources remain unrecorded rather than guessed.
- **Discounts** — What to use it for: Discounts represented on issued invoices. What to watch: Read the disclosure about which line discounts are included.
- **Stock Movement** — What to use it for: Stock changes across products in a period. What to watch: Each quantity has its own product unit.
- **Job Profitability** — What to use it for: Job selling values and costs. What to watch: Cost and employee-pay access can withhold figures.
- **Parts Profitability** — What to use it for: Parts selling values and costs. What to watch: Stock shortfalls and estimated costs need review.

## What happens next

Use the report to identify records needing investigation, then open the original job, invoice, customer or product. Exporting a report does not change those records.

## Troubleshooting

A missing report can be a specific report-permission restriction. Blank or withheld cost is not zero. If totals differ, compare job date, invoice date and payment date, and check whether the report includes drafts, packages or actual money movements.

[Screenshot: All Reports showing operational and financial report choices; avoid real business totals.]

guides.title: Read financial reports and account statements
guides.body:
Financial reports distinguish bills raised, money received, costs incurred and money paid. Choose the report that matches the question rather than treating every total as cash in the bank.

## Profit & Loss

Open **Reports → Profit & Loss**, choose the period and read the notes. Revenue uses issued invoice amounts excluding recorded VAT. Expenses and other income also use their amounts excluding recorded VAT.

Revenue follows invoice dates while job costs can follow job dates. A repair crossing a month end can therefore place its cost and revenue in different periods. Pending expenses can count as costs before cash is paid.

## Balance Snapshot

Open **Reports → Balance Snapshot** and choose the as-of date. Cash/bank, receivables and payables have their own calculation basis. Later-dated payments are not treated as if they happened before the selected date.

The stock-at-cost figure uses current remaining stock records; it is not a full reconstruction of physical stock for every historical date. Read that limitation before comparing old snapshots.

## Payment Types

Open **Reports → Payment Types** and select the period. This groups recorded money movements by method and account. Deposit and gift-card redemption can settle an invoice without new cash, so they are not equivalent to a new cash receipt in this report.

## Customer and supplier statements

1. Open **Customer Statement** or **Supplier Statement** under Reports.
2. Select the account and date range.
3. Review opening balance, dated bills/receipts, running balance and ageing.
4. Compare disputed entries with their original documents before exporting the statement.

Customer wallet top-ups are separate from unpaid invoices. Supplier liabilities include received purchases; pending or ordered purchases are not treated as received stock bills. Fleet consolidation should not be added again to workshop sales totals.

## Troubleshooting

Check dates, issue/receipt status, voids and reversals first. Report access and cost/payroll access may hide some figures. A statement discrepancy should be investigated, not corrected by inserting an unrelated payment or editing a historical starting balance.

## Related articles

- [Payment accounts and ledger](/help/en/autoserv-pro/payment-accounts-and-ledger)
- [Review VAT and tax figures](/help/en/autoserv-pro/review-vat-and-tax-figures)

guides.title: Review tax on documents and the VAT report
guides.body:
SAM records tax amounts on invoices, received purchases and expenses. This guide explains the product's figures; your business must still confirm the appropriate treatment for its transactions.

## Check an invoice before issue

1. Review the customer's and workshop's relevant billing details.
2. Check product-line tax and the fallback **VAT Rate** on the invoice.
3. Review discounts, shipping, tax totals and **Grand Total**.
4. Resolve any incorrect amount before **Issue**, because issued lines are locked.

Do not assume the displayed UAE default applies to every customer, workshop or supply. Tax is part of the document review, not a setting to change merely to force a preferred total.

## Check purchasing and expenses

On a purchase, compare the line tax and grand total with the supplier's document. On an expense, **Amount (incl. VAT)** is the full amount and **Of which VAT** is the tax already contained within it; it is not added again.

## Open the report

1. Open **Compliance → VAT Return**.
2. Choose the reporting period.
3. Review the output figures from issued invoices and the input figures from received purchases and recorded expenses.
4. Read all legacy-record and treatment disclosures.
5. Export the report if needed for your normal review process.

Older records may have recorded tax totals without the same detailed treatment breakdown as new records. They are disclosed separately rather than silently assigned to a new category. Editing an old purchase is not a way to invent historical input tax.

## What happens next

The report supplies figures for review. Generating or downloading it does not submit a tax return. An available **Peppol XML** invoice download is a document export; it does not by itself prove delivery to or acceptance by an external authority or network.

## Troubleshooting

Compare the period, issue status, purchase receipt status and stored tax amounts. Do not add fleet consolidated totals a second time to the underlying workshop invoice amounts.

guides.title: Give a customer access to their portal
guides.body:
The customer portal lets a vehicle owner view their own workshop records. It uses a separate customer login; it is not an employee account or the Orions360 Support Hub staff login.

## Set up access as workshop staff

1. Open the correct customer record and check their email address.
2. Use **Set Portal Password**.
3. Enter **New Password** and **Confirm Password**, then save through the dialog. The portal-password setting requires at least six characters; choose a stronger password suitable for your customer-access process.
4. Obtain the **Portal Login URL** from **Configuration → Company Settings**.
5. Share the customer's access details privately and explain that this is the workshop customer portal.

Setting a password is the access mechanism in this workflow. Do not look for an assumed **Portal Access Enabled** checkbox on the customer form.

## Use the portal as a customer

1. Open the workshop's portal address.
2. Enter the email address recorded by the workshop and your portal password.
3. Use the dashboard and available **Work Orders**, **Invoices** and **Vehicles** pages to review your records.
4. Open a specific record for more information, or use **Profile** for the available contact/password updates.

## What happens next

You can review records associated with your customer account. Viewing a document does not authorise new work or make a payment. For a new visit, use the workshop's booking link or contact the team.

## Troubleshooting

If sign-in fails, ask the workshop to confirm the recorded email and reset the portal password. A staff password-reset link is not a portal password reset. If an invoice or advance amount looks inconsistent, ask staff to check the issued invoice and full payment history rather than relying solely on the portal summary.

guides.title: Handle a walk-in from reception to payment
guides.body:
Use this workflow when a vehicle arrives without an appointment. It follows the same repair and billing controls as a booked visit.

## Before the vehicle enters the workshop

1. Search **Customers** and **Vehicles**. Match the plate and owner rather than creating duplicates.
2. Create any missing customer and vehicle records with verified contact details.
3. Open **Work Orders → Add Work Order** and record the complaint, mileage, advisor, promised date and coverage.
4. **Save**, then add intake photos and an inspection where appropriate.

If a scan or quick-intake flow uses a general walk-in customer, replace or confirm the actual customer association before sharing private links or issuing documents.

## Agree and perform the work

1. If the price is not yet agreed, prepare an estimate and obtain the customer's agreement.
2. Create or convert the job order and check tasks, packages, parts and prices.
3. Use **Approve Cost** through an authorised colleague.
4. Assign the vehicle to a bay and assign technicians to the work.
5. Record work with timers and completion actions. If parts are missing, follow the request and purchasing process rather than marking the work finished.
6. Perform quality review and use **Approve Work**.

## Bill and hand over

1. Use **Add Invoice** and check the final work, discounts, tax and any advance.
2. **Save as Draft** for review or **Issue** when final.
3. Record the amount actually received using **Record Payment**. Leave a balance for any unpaid portion.
4. Give the customer the appropriate invoice or receipt.
5. Confirm collection and release the bay when the vehicle leaves. Check the work-order status; an Invoiced status is terminal in the editor, so do not try to force it back through the repair stages.

## What happens next

The visit, work, billing and receipts form a connected history. A return visit should be reviewed as a new service event or warranty case, not hidden by rewriting an issued job.

- [Create and manage work orders](/help/en/autoserv-pro/create-and-manage-work-orders)

guides.title: Turn inspection findings into an agreed repair
guides.body:
This workflow helps an advisor explain a problem, obtain agreement and hand the work to technicians. An inspection finding, a customer decision and a staff approval each mean something different.

## Record and explain the findings

1. Open the work order and use **Start inspection**.
2. Choose the right checklist and record findings, measurements and suitable photographs.
3. Use **Save** while still preparing the record. **Complete inspection** freezes it; start a new inspection for a later re-check.
4. Use **Share with customer** after checking what the link exposes.

## Prepare the quote

1. Use **Estimate from findings** when genuine items are marked Attention or Fail.
2. Open the resulting estimate. The generated lines need pricing: review their descriptions, hours and rates, then add appropriate parts or packages.
3. Save and inspect the full proposed amount.
4. Use **Send** and check whether the approval link was delivered or only copied.

If there are several quotes on the same visit, verify which work the customer is seeing before asking for agreement. When a quote changes, confirm that the customer's decision refers to the revised scope and amount.

## Start authorised work

1. Review the customer's response and any separate discussion.
2. If the customer declines, discuss the next step; do not convert simply to clear a pending item.
3. Once agreed, use **Convert to JO**.
4. Review the job order, use **Approve Cost** through the authorised colleague and assign technicians.
5. Complete the work, perform quality review and use **Approve Work** before the normal invoice step.

## What happens next

The agreed repair proceeds through the job workflow. Customer acceptance does not itself finish the repair, issue an invoice or take payment.

## Troubleshooting

No flagged findings means there is nothing for the automatic estimate action to quote. A zero-priced generated task needs review, not immediate sending. If an approval page shows unexpected work, pause and ask the administrator to resolve the visit/quote association.

## Related articles

- [Inspect a vehicle](/help/en/autoserv-pro/inspect-a-vehicle)

guides.title: Replenish missing parts and continue the job
guides.body:
Use this workflow when a saved job or technician request identifies a stock shortfall. A saved backorder is not a promise that the part is on the shelf.

## Confirm what is missing

1. Open the job and review the warning, product, quantity and unit.
2. Compare the product's **On hand**, **Available** and **In use** figures with its stock history.
3. Check whether a package already includes the item or another line has allocated it.
4. Have the technician submit **Request Parts** for the genuinely needed quantity.

## Order and receive

1. The storekeeper reviews the request and uses **Mark Ordered** when procurement is needed.
2. Create the supplier purchase separately. Enter the correct pack, quantity, unit cost and tax.
3. Leave the purchase Ordered while waiting.
4. When the delivery arrives, compare it with the supplier document, set the purchase **Received** and save.
5. Check the resulting available quantity and unit conversion.

## Issue and reconcile

1. Reopen the parts request and use **Approve** once stock covers it.
2. Hand over the parts and use **Mark Issued**.
3. Ask the technician to acknowledge receipt where available.
4. Review the original job lines and any backorder/cost indicators with the advisor. Do not add a duplicate charge for a part already present on the job.
5. Resume the work, complete it and obtain work approval before billing.

## What happens next

The delivery, request and job each record a different part of the process. Receiving stock does not automatically finish the repair, settle the supplier or prove that every earlier estimated cost has been reconciled.

## Troubleshooting

If approval still reports a shortfall, check received status, compatible units and other jobs using the stock. A count adjustment should only reflect a verified physical correction, not be used to manufacture availability for approval.

guides.title: Understand staff roles and permissions
guides.body:
A role groups permissions. Your workshop can customise roles, so a role name alone does not guarantee access. The table describes the current default staff presets; older or customised workshops can differ.

- **System Admin** — Typical default responsibilities: Full workshop administration. Important boundary: Use a personal account rather than sharing this login.
- **Service Manager** — Typical default responsibilities: Workshop supervision, approvals, invoicing, finance, stock, reports and employees. Important boundary: Not every system-setting or role-administration permission is part of the manager preset.
- **Service Advisor** — Typical default responsibilities: Customers, vehicles, visits, estimates, job preparation, assignment and invoice drafts/payments. Important boundary: Invoice issue, cost approval, work approval and rework are not all included by default.
- **Receptionist** — Typical default responsibilities: Customer/vehicle intake, work-order creation and booking visibility. Important boundary: Viewing bookings does not include managing them by default.
- **Technician** — Typical default responsibilities: Assigned work, timers, relevant inspections and parts requests. Important boundary: The technician workflow is not unrestricted job editing or access to everyone's pay.
- **Cashier** — Typical default responsibilities: Invoice preparation, approval, issue, sending and payments; selected finance/report access. Important boundary: Transfers, reversals and supplier payments are separate responsibilities.

Other role names, including Service Writer, Store Manager and Warranty Manager, may exist. Have the administrator inspect their actual permissions rather than assuming a preset from the name.

## Review or change access

1. An authorised administrator opens **Configuration → Users** and reviews the person's **Roles**.
2. Open **Configuration → Roles** to inspect the chosen role's **Permissions**.
3. Use **Edit**, select only the responsibilities intended for that role, and **Save**.
4. Recheck the person's available actions after the access change.

Changing a role can affect every user assigned to it. A staff login and an employee/technician record also need to be correctly linked for assignment and timers.

## Permissions that should not be confused

- Viewing a record is separate from creating, editing or deleting it.
- **Approve Cost**, **Approve Work**, rework and hour overrides are separate job actions.
- Invoice drafting, approval, issue, sending and payments are separate responsibilities.
- Finance recording, transfers, supplier payments and reversals are separate.
- Inspection recording, completion and sharing are separate.
- Cost figures, employee compensation and individual reports can have additional access checks.
- Campaign preparation does not automatically include campaign sending.

## Troubleshooting

A feature can require both permission and a plan entitlement. Sami follows the same access boundaries. If a menu is visible but the action is refused, report the exact page and message to the administrator rather than granting broad access just to remove the error.

## Related articles

guides.title: Fix login, missing-menu and access problems
guides.body:
Start by identifying whether the problem is the login, staff permissions or workshop subscription. These require different fixes.

## I cannot sign in

1. Check that you are opening your workshop's staff login, not a different workshop or the customer portal.
2. Confirm the email address with your administrator.
3. Use **Forgot Password?** if you cannot recall the staff password.
4. For an employee invitation, use the newest access link. It works once and expires after 48 hours.

If email does not arrive, check spam and ask the administrator to inspect email settings and logs. Do not repeatedly create staff accounts for the same person.

## I signed in, but a menu or action is missing

1. Ask the administrator to review your effective role permissions.
2. Check whether the action needs more than viewing access—for example, booking management or invoice issue.
3. Check whether the workshop's plan includes the feature.
4. Refresh your session after an authorised access change.

Technicians normally see **My Work** rather than the complete advisor navigation. A hidden salary or cost figure is an access restriction, not a zero value.

## I can read records but cannot save

An expired trial can block writes while leaving reads available. An eligible administrator can review **Plan & Billing** and the extension or upgrade options. A suspended account requires support assistance.

If only one old record refuses changes, check its status: an issued invoice, invoiced job or completed inspection may be deliberately locked.

## If the problem continues

Provide support with the workshop address, page, time, exact error and action you were trying to perform. Include your role name if known. Do not send passwords, access links or provider keys.

## Related articles

- [Roles and permissions](/help/en/autoserv-pro/roles-and-permissions)

guides.title: Fix booking, job, timer and stock problems
guides.body:
Use the checks below before repeating an action. A slow response does not always mean that nothing was saved.

- **No booking slots** — What it means: The chosen date has no currently offered capacity. What to check next: Active weekdays, holidays, passed times and full slots.
- **Slot just became fully booked** — What it means: Another request used the remaining capacity. What to check next: Choose another slot; do not keep resubmitting the same one.
- **Unsure whether a booking converted** — What it means: A work order may already exist. What to check next: Search the booking and Work Orders before converting again.
- **No technician profile** — What it means: Your login is not linked to an appropriate employee. What to check next: Ask the administrator to check the employee/user link.
- **Technician missing from assignment** — What it means: Job title alone is insufficient. What to check next: Confirm the linked user has the Technician role.
- **Another timer is running** — What it means: A technician can clock one task or package at a time. What to check next: Stop or finish the named work before starting another.
- **Cost must be approved** — What it means: Work approval was attempted too early. What to check next: Obtain genuine price agreement and authorised cost approval.
- **Job is invoiced and locked** — What it means: Billing has finalised this job. What to check next: Ask the billing administrator; do not try rework to bypass the lock.
- **Inspection is complete** — What it means: Its findings are frozen. What to check next: Start a new inspection for a re-check.
- **Nothing was flagged** — What it means: No Attention or Fail findings exist. What to check next: Review the real findings; do not create a false failure.
- **Saved with a stock shortfall** — What it means: The job saved but required parts are missing. What to check next: Check available stock and follow purchasing/request steps.
- **Unit is not in the product's family** — What it means: The measurements cannot be converted. What to check next: Select a compatible stock, pack or consumption unit.

## Stock still looks wrong

Open the product's **Stock history**. Compare its unit, opening quantity, received purchases, adjustments and allocated job/estimate lines. Do not enter both opening stock and a received purchase for the same starting quantity.

## If the problem continues

Keep the job, work-order, booking or product reference and the exact error. Ask the responsible manager to inspect the original records before deleting, resetting or adding compensating transactions.

## Related articles

- [Replenish parts for a job](/help/en/autoserv-pro/replenish-parts-for-a-job)

guides.title: Fix invoice and payment problems
guides.body:
Investigate the existing document before creating another invoice or payment. A correction must preserve what actually happened.

## The job does not appear when adding an invoice

Check the selected customer, work approval and whether the job has already been invoiced. Use the appropriate colleague for missing approval or issue permission. A copied or provisional document is not a replacement for the normal invoice flow.

## The invoice is locked

Issued invoice lines are final. The associated job is also locked. Ask the billing administrator to determine the appropriate correction process; do not delete the job or create an unexplained second invoice. This guide does not assume a credit-note button exists.

## The payment amount exceeds the balance

1. Reopen the invoice and review **Payments Received**.
2. Check **Advance Applied**, **Paid** and **Balance Due**.
3. Confirm whether an online payment or another colleague's receipt has already been recorded.
4. Enter only the actual remaining amount received.

For bulk payment, each allocation must fit its invoice and the allocations must match the receipt total.

## The save timed out

Reload the invoice and payment history before retrying. If the invoice was issued but the payment was not recorded, use **Record Payment** on that invoice rather than creating it again. For provider payments, keep the provider reference and ask support to reconcile it before charging again.

## The statement differs from the portal or dashboard

Compare the date range, invoice status and included advances. A customer wallet top-up is different from unpaid debt. Fleet consolidated bills should not be counted as additional workshop sales. Portal summaries may not show the same detail as the full staff invoice and statement.

## If the problem continues

Provide the document reference, amount, method, payment date and exact error. Share only the minimum supporting information needed; never include full card details or credentials.

## Related articles

- [Record invoice payments](/help/en/autoserv-pro/record-invoice-payments)
- [Financial reports and statements](/help/en/autoserv-pro/financial-reports-and-statements)

guides.title: Fix email, WhatsApp, shared-link and print problems
guides.body:
A business record can save even when its notification fails. Check the record first so that retrying a message does not duplicate the underlying work or payment.

## An email did not arrive

1. Confirm the recipient address on the customer or employee record.
2. Check the recipient's spam folder.
3. Ask an authorised administrator to open **Email Settings → Send Logs**.
4. Check that the intended template is enabled and the correct mail connection is active.
5. Use **Check connection** for SMTP and a separate **Send test email** to an address you control.

Connection success checks access to the mail service; it does not guarantee that a customer's mailbox accepted the message.

## WhatsApp says the link was copied

Read the full result. It may say the customer has no phone number or the provider did not send. Open the copied link to verify the intended record, then paste it into the correct customer conversation. Copying is not sending.

If automated sending keeps failing, check the active provider, sending number, credentials, permitted destinations and any configured templates. A phone's WhatsApp Business app alone does not configure SAM's provider connection.

## A shared page is expired or incorrect

Ask staff to reopen the source record and obtain the correct current link. Employee access links work once and expire after 48 hours. Document-share links display their own expiry. Never change random parts of a link to find a different customer's document.

If an estimate link shows unexpected work, pause approval and ask the administrator to check the quote linked to the visit.

## A PDF or print preview is blank

Reopen the document, wait for the preview and check the chosen template and language. If the generated PDF remains incomplete, contact support with the reference and settings. Do not issue or delete another invoice to solve a rendering problem.

## Related articles

guides.title: SAM frequently asked questions
guides.body:
## Do I need an appointment before opening a work order?

No. Create a work order directly for a walk-in, or convert an existing service booking when the vehicle arrives.

## Can one customer have several vehicles?

Yes. Add each vehicle under the correct customer and select the relevant vehicle for each visit.

## Are a work order and a job order the same?

No. The work order represents the visit; job orders contain its tasks, packages, parts and technician work. A visit can have more than one job order.

## Does submitting the booking form mean staff confirmed the appointment?

The request is saved, but staff confirmation is separate. Keep the booking reference and check with the workshop before travelling if confirmation is important.

## Can I edit an estimate after sending it?

An uninvoiced estimate can be edited with the appropriate permission. If its scope or price changes, verify what the customer sees and obtain agreement to the revised work before proceeding.

## Does customer approval automatically finish or invoice a job?

No. Customer agreement, **Convert to JO**, staff **Approve Cost**, technician work, **Approve Work**, invoice issue and payment are separate stages.

## Can I convert a rejected estimate?

The editor can offer **Convert anyway**. Use it only if the customer has subsequently agreed, for example by phone or in person.

## Can I add parts after a job starts?

An uninvoiced job can be edited by an authorised person. Review stock, the changed price and customer agreement before saving. An invoiced job is locked.

## Why did stock change when I saved work?

Saved job and estimate parts/package lines can affect stock availability in the current workflow. Review the stock history and avoid duplicate lines.

## Does Mark Ordered receive stock?

No. Record and receive the actual supplier purchase. A parts-request status is not a purchase receipt.

## Can I run two technician timers?

No. Stop or finish the running task or package before starting another.

## Does rework erase all history?

No. It reopens the job's tasks, withdraws work approval and resets task actual-hour values. Past time sessions remain for reporting. Review hours and costs after rework.

## Can I record a partial payment?

Yes, on an issued invoice. Enter the amount received; the remainder stays due.

## Can I take money before invoicing?

Use a work-order advance. Eligible advances are applied when the invoice is issued. Do not record the same receipt twice.

## Is a customer deposit the same as an advance?

No. Customer deposits use a separate wallet mechanism. Ask the administrator to review its current balance and redemption workflow before using it.

## Can I change or delete an issued invoice to correct it?

Issued lines and the billed job are locked. Ask the billing administrator for the correction process; do not delete supporting work or create an unexplained replacement.

## Does recording Card charge the customer's card?

A manually recorded payment method describes a receipt. It does not charge a card. **Pay Online**, when enabled, uses the configured provider flow.

## Do customers need staff logins to see progress?

No. Shared tracking, inspection and document links are customer-facing. The customer portal also has its own separate login.

## Why can my colleague see a button that I cannot?

Your permissions, role, plan or the record's status may differ. Viewing a record does not grant every action on it.

## Are hidden costs or salaries zero?

No. They may be withheld from your account. Ask the authorised manager to review them.

## Does downloading the VAT report submit a return?

No. It produces figures for review. A report or XML download is not a submission or acceptance confirmation.

## Can Sami bypass an approval or permission?

No. Supported action drafts still require your confirmation and the applicable product permissions and checks.

guides.title: Import labour tasks and export workshop data
guides.body:
SAM supports a labour-task spreadsheet import and exports on supported lists and reports. An export creates a file; an import creates catalogue records.

## Prepare a labour-task spreadsheet

Use XLSX, XLS or CSV, no larger than 5 MB. Put these headings in the first row exactly as shown by **Import Labor Tasks**:

- **`task_code`** — A unique task code.
- **`task_name`** — The customer-friendly task name.
- **`normal_rate`** — A non-negative normal rate.
- **`warranty_rate`** — The warranty rate.
- **`task_hour`** — Estimated hours.

Use one task per row. Existing task codes are skipped rather than overwritten. Check for duplicate codes within the file too.

## Import the file

1. Open **Workshop → Labour Tasks** and its import action.
2. Read the headings shown in **Import Labor Tasks**.
3. Use **Choose file…**, select the prepared spreadsheet and run the import.
4. Review the imported/skipped summary and any row errors.
5. Search the catalogue for representative tasks and check their rates and hours.

Valid rows can import even when other rows fail. Correct the rejected rows and review the resulting catalogue before repeating the import. The action requires labour-task management access.

## Export a list or report

1. Open the required list or report and set its search, date and status filters.
2. Use the available export control and select one of the offered formats, such as PDF, Excel or CSV.
3. Open the downloaded file and confirm the period, columns and totals before sharing it.

Available formats depend on the screen. Do not assume a single-page view means the export contains only that page. Export permissions and cost/payroll restrictions still apply.

## Backup versus export

**Company Settings → Download a backup** produces a broader copy of records and uploaded files. Keep that ZIP under business control. A report export is a selected view and is not a complete restore-ready workshop backup.

guides.title: Start using SAM: free trial, demo and setup for a new workshop
guides.body:
This guide is for a workshop that does not have SAM (Smart Auto Manager) yet. It explains how to start the free trial yourself, what the trial includes, and how to ask to be shown SAM first.

## Who this is for

Use this guide if your workshop has no SAM account. You do not need an invitation. You can create the workshop account yourself.

If your workshop already uses SAM and you only need a login, go to the last section of this guide.

## Start the free trial yourself

1. Open [https://app.autoshopstack.com/register](https://app.autoshopstack.com/register). You can also open [https://app.autoshopstack.com](https://app.autoshopstack.com) and select **Start 14-day free trial** or **Create your workshop**.
2. Enter your **Workshop Name**.
3. Choose **Your Workshop URL**. This is your workshop's address. It ends in `.autoshopstack.com`.
4. Under **Admin account**, enter **Your Name**, **Email Address**, **Password** and **Confirm Password**. The password needs at least 8 characters.
5. Under **How do you want to start?**, choose one option:
   - **With sample data** — pre-loaded vehicles, job cards and invoices to explore.
   - **Blank workshop** — start clean.
6. Select **Start Free Trial**.

No credit card is required.

Keep your workshop URL, email address and password. You need them to sign in. When you are ready to run a real job, follow [Your first workshop job](/help/en/autoserv-pro/first-workshop-job).

## What the free trial includes

- It lasts 14 days.
- No credit card is required.
- You can extend it once, by 14 more days. [Plans, trials and billing](/help/en/autoserv-pro/plans-trials-and-billing) explains when the extension is offered.

It is a capped trial. During the trial, one workshop can have up to:

- 100 work orders
- 150 job orders
- 50 customers
- 100 vehicles
- 5 staff
- 100 invoices
- 10 questions to Sami, shared by the whole workshop

Accounting, fleet and insurance are read-only during the trial. You can view them, but you cannot add or change records.

## Prefer to be shown first?

You do not have to start alone. The Orions360 founders can give you a demo and set SAM up at your garage, with your workshop's lists loaded and your team trained.

- Lists are things like your customers, vehicles and parts.
- Past invoices, job history and photos stay in your old system.
- If you are in Abu Dhabi, the founders come to your garage. If you are elsewhere, ask for a demo on a call.

To ask for a demo or a setup visit, reply on WhatsApp.
